A genuine mismatch normalizes via a new private helper `app._evaluate_procurement_currency_threshold` (a deliberate, disclosed variant of PRC-258's own `app._normalize_vendor_comparison_currency`) composing `app.convert_finance_amount`. Per this entry's own explicit reasoning ("under-routing... the more dangerous direction"), any conversion-unavailable outcome -- missing FX rate, unsupported currency, OR the actor lacking `FIN:View` -- FAILS CLOSED (`required=true`, reason `value_currency_unverifiable_defaulted_to_required`) rather than silently skipping governance; the whole-transaction abort risk that fail-closed choice could otherwise cause for a caller like `app.create_rate_version` (whose own authority model is `is_support_grant_authority`, unrelated to `FIN:View`) is handled by catching `insufficient_privilege` inside the new helper rather than letting it propagate. `app._request_procurement_entity_approval` threads its own already-received `p_currency` into the evaluator's new parameter -- no entity-type submit RPC (`rate_version`/`purchase_order`/`vendor_selection`) needed to change. Regression evidence: `scripts/db-tests/procurement-approval.sql`, six new test blocks proving (a) same-currency unaffected even for an actor with zero FIN permissions, (b) real cross-currency normalization both directions via the full `app.create_rate_version` chain, (c) `purchase_order`/`vendor_selection` normalize identically (including one direct-through-`_request_procurement_entity_approval` proof), (d) fail-closed on missing FIN:View with the full transaction committing, (e) fail-closed on a missing FX rate, (f) `vendor_contract`/`vendor_activation`/`exception_override` structurally cannot reach the new code path at all (`min_value_amount` can never be set for them, unchanged `procurement_approval_policies_value_dimension_check`). | Yes -- a tenant that publishes a rate_version/vendor_selection policy today gets a currency-blind threshold; a rate or selection denominated in a low-value-per-unit currency can cross a threshold meant for a high-value-per-unit currency (over-routing) or vice versa (under-routing, the more dangerous direction: a large IDR-denominated value could silently skip governance review if a policy was tuned assuming USD-scale numbers). Should be resolved before any tenant is told procurement governance thresholds are currency-aware |

## 4. Issue records

### ISS-2026-002 — Parallel-session collision (no single-writer discipline)

Two sessions ran Prompt 21 concurrently on separate branches (`…-oanf5a`, `…-b492y3`); both merged to `main` and the merge corrupted the discovery baseline and duplicated the context set (see `ERROR_LEDGER.md` ERR-2026-001). Root cause: no lock/convention preventing concurrent execution of the same runtime step. **Handling:** designate one authoritative build branch per runtime step; do not launch parallel agent sessions on the same step; a future prompt must verify checkpoint lineage before writing. Status `OPEN` until a written single-writer convention is adopted (candidate: note in `AGENTS.md`).

**Recurrence (2026-07-14, third session):** a third branch, `claude/eloquent-mayer-s40hn4`, was cut from `main` at `d587445` *before* this reconciliation (`CG-S2-DISC-001-R1`) had merged. It independently discovered the same underlying corruption and — not knowing about `-R1` — resolved it the opposite way (root-level context kept canonical, `docs/runtime/*` marked superseded) while also completing Step 2 discovery Prompts 22–34. On merge with `main`, that branch's canonical-location choice was reverted in favor of this ratified decision (`docs/runtime/` canonical); its Step 2 discovery deliverables (Prompts 22–34, `docs/discovery/02_*.md`–`14_*.md`) were kept and layered on top of the reconciled baseline (see `TASK_LEDGER.md` `CG-S2-DISC-002..014` and `CHANGE_MANIFEST.md` `CHG-2026-003`). This is the second occurrence of this exact issue and reinforces that it remains `OPEN` until a single-writer convention is actually enforced, not just documented.

**Recurrence (2026-07-15, fourth occurrence — reconciliation never actually performed):** a fourth branch, `claude/sleepy-ride-4vxsk6`, diverged from `origin/main`@`27389a4` (PR #8, Prompt 45) and independently executed Prompts 46–51, Phase 0 kickoff (80), and Prompts 81–82 — nine commits, three full architecture documents, a full Phase 0 kickoff, and two Phase 0 capability prompts — in parallel with this branch (`agent/cargogrid-autonomous-build`) doing the equivalent Prompts 49–51/80/81. That branch opened GitHub PR #10 15 seconds after this branch's PR #9 merged into `main`, confirming near-simultaneous parallel execution. The two lineages' outputs for the same task IDs materially differ (e.g. 607 vs. 401 traced requirement items for the "same" Prompt 49/CG-S3-ARCH-014 output). A prior session halted further Phase 0 execution on discovering it and recorded `BLOCKED_WORKTREE` in `HANDOFF.md`, pending an explicit operator decision among three reconciliation options. Full detail: `ERROR_LEDGER.md` `ERR-2026-002`.

**Recurrence (2026-07-15, fifth occurrence — corruption now committed to `main`, escalated to Sev-1):** without that operator decision ever being recorded, PR #10 and then PR #11 (this run's designated branch) were both merged into `main` (`a8a197f`, `b7653cb`). Because neither merge produced git conflict markers (both lineages' edits were pure insertions relative to their shared base), git silently concatenated both divergent lineages' full content into the same files. `docs/architecture/14_REQUIREMENT_PHASE_TRACEABILITY.md`, `15_RISK_RANKED_CRITICAL_PATH.md`, and `16_STEP3_CLOSURE_REPORT.md` each now contain two complete, contradictory copies of the same document (confirmed: two `## 1.` sections in each, 607-item vs. 401-item traceability totals). `docs/runtime/HANDOFF.md`, `CARGOGRID_BUILD_STATUS.md`, and `TASK_LEDGER.md` show the same stacking pattern for narrative/status content. Full detail and evidence: `ERROR_LEDGER.md` `ERR-2026-003`. This is the clearest evidence yet that `ISS-2026-002` needs an *enforced* single-writer lock (e.g. a pre-flight check in each routine invocation that fails fast if any other open PR/branch already claims the current task-ID range, and a rule that merging a PR while a sibling PR covering the same task-ID range is still open requires explicit reconciliation, not a fast-forward/no-conflict merge) — a documented convention has now been silently violated five times.

**Resolution of the 5th-occurrence corruption (2026-07-15):** the operator authorized adopting **Lineage A** as authoritative. `docs/architecture/14..16_*.md` were rewritten as single coherent Lineage A documents (607-item baseline), Prompt 82 was re-verified against it, and the duplicate Phase 0 build logs were consolidated onto the singular prompt-package path. `ERR-2026-003` is `RECOVERED`. This cleared the *content* corruption and unblocked Phase 0.

**Enforcement adopted (2026-07-15, `CG-S5-PH0-008`, Prompt 87 — closes the *process* gap):** `docs/git/GIT_STRATEGY.md` §7 documents, and `AGENTS.md`'s "Required pre-flight" section now mandates, a two-part pre-flight collision check before starting any Phase 0+ prompt: (1) list open PRs/branches via the GitHub API/MCP and stop if another session claims the same task-ID range — **executed for real this checkpoint**: zero open PRs, and the only branch with commits ahead of `origin/main` is this session's own `agent/cargogrid-autonomous-build` (`claude/sleepy-ride-8pg1em`, this session's harness-assigned branch, is fully contained in `origin/main` — confirmed via `git merge-base`, not assumed); (2) `pnpm run git:check` (`scripts/git/check-worktree-collision.ts`, 4 passing tests) automates the locally-checkable half — a genuine fork between two `agent/*`/`claude/*` branches (each having commits the other lacks), the exact `ERR-2026-002`/`ERR-2026-003` precondition. **Status `RESOLVED`**: this is now a documented, followed, and partially-automated procedure rather than an unenforced convention silently skipped five times — no further action required unless a 6th occurrence demonstrates the procedure itself is insufficient.

### ISS-2026-007 — `pnpm audit` calls a retired npm endpoint (OPEN, Medium)

Discovered `2026-07-15` during `CG-S5-PH0-015` (Prompt 94, Security Baseline Controls). Running `pnpm audit` against this repository's real, current lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`) failed with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_BAD_RESPONSE`: both `registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick` and `registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/security/audits` responded `410 Gone` — "This endpoint is being retired. Use the bulk advisory endpoint instead" (exact error captured this checkpoint, `docs/standards/SECURITY_STANDARDS.md` §5). `npm audit` was attempted as a fallback and requires a `package-lock.json`, which this repository deliberately does not carry (`ADR-0002`) — generating a second, non-authoritative lockfile solely to audit was rejected as a worse outcome. **Handling:** no CI gate was wired for this — either a hard-fail (blocks every future PR for an upstream endpoint problem, not a real dependency vulnerability) or a soft-pass via `--ignore-registry-errors` (a fabricated "audited, clean" signal with no real subject) would violate this repository's own established "never fabricate a passing gate" discipline (`docs/build-log/phase-00/PH0-88.md` §3). **What remains a real control:** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (already wired in CI since `PH0-88`) still guarantees deterministic, lockfile-pinned installs — this issue is specifically about the *absence of automated vulnerability-database checking*, not about install determinism. **Status `OPEN`**, Medium severity (a real, disclosed gap in supply-chain evidence, though no specific vulnerability is known or suspected) — re-attempt owner: DevEx, once pnpm ships bulk-advisory-endpoint support (pnpm `11.13.1` is available upstream as of this checkpoint, but upgrading the pinned major version is out of `PH0-94`'s scope, Prompt 94 §12's "no broad dependency upgrade"; GitHub's native Dependabot alerts are a viable interim signal but enabling them is a repository-settings change, not a code change, and was not performed unilaterally this checkpoint).

### ISS-2026-008 — `check-secrets.ts`'s generic-assignment pattern is narrower than sibling foundations' PII coverage (RESOLVED, Low)

Discovered `2026-07-16` during `CG-S5-PH0-020` (Prompt 99, Phase 0 Integrated Verification), via `scripts/verification/phase0-integration.test.ts`'s cross-foundation sensitive-key-pattern consistency suite — a test that runs the *same* representative key names (`password`, `npwp`, `bankAccountNumber`, `salary`) through all three independently-authored pattern lists together, something no single module's own isolated test suite (each written at a different prior checkpoint — `PH0-93`, `PH0-94`, `PH0-97`) could have caught on its own. Result: `scripts/observability/logger.ts`'s `redact()` and `scripts/product-analytics/analytics.ts`'s `findProhibitedProperties()` both correctly flag all four representative keys; `scripts/security/check-secrets.ts`'s `GENERIC_HARDCODED_SECRET_ASSIGNMENT` pattern (`secret|password|token|api[_-]?key|private[_-]?key`) flags only `password`, not `npwp`/`bankAccountNumber`/`salary`. Prompt 99 explicitly deferred the scope judgment call to a dedicated task rather than deciding it unilaterally during verification (§11: "default no repair").

**Resolved `2026-07-16` during `CG-S5-PH0-021` (Prompt 100, Phase 0 Hardening)** — the dedicated task Prompt 99 named. Decision: **keep `check-secrets.ts` scoped to credential shapes; do not widen it to general PII detection.** Rationale: (1) industry-standard secret scanners (gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets) target key/token/password shapes, not arbitrary PII — widening the scope would make `check-secrets.ts` a second, overlapping PII scanner, which Prompt 100 §24's "no new capability" rule forbids; (2) this repository already has three real, tested, purpose-built PII-handling mechanisms for their own respective data-flow surfaces — `scripts/data-classification/registry.ts`/`check-registry.ts` (schema-field classification), `scripts/product-analytics/analytics.ts` (event-property rejection), `scripts/observability/logger.ts` (log-field redaction) — so a hardcoded PII literal in source is correctly out of `check-secrets.ts`'s lane, not an uncovered risk; (3) a real PII value should never be a literal in tracked source regardless of its key name, which is a code-review/data-classification concern, not a key-name-pattern-matching one. **Evidence:** `docs/standards/SECURITY_STANDARDS.md` §3 now states this boundary explicitly; `scripts/security/check-secrets.ts` carries a one-line scope comment; `scripts/verification/phase0-integration.test.ts`'s dedicated test was rewritten from "documents a disclosed gap" to "proves the intentional boundary holds in both directions" (asserts `check-secrets.ts` still does not match the PII-shaped keys, and that `logger.ts` still redacts them regardless — the PII-handling responsibility is proven to land somewhere, not merely absent from one module). Full detail: `docs/build-log/phase-00/PH0-100.md`. **Status `RESOLVED`** — a documented design boundary, not a defect; no code behavior changed, `pnpm run security:check` still reports zero findings.

### ISS-2026-053 — `app.enqueue_job` (PLT-132)'s idempotency replay matches the key but never verifies the target tuple (OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-08` during `CG-S11-PRC-017` (Prompt 266, Procurement Dashboard and Reports), while implementing `app.enqueue_procurement_report_export`. `app.enqueue_job` (`supabase/migrations/20260719180000_create_background_job_framework.sql`, PLT-132) accepts an `idempotency_key` and, on a replay with the same key, returns the existing `app.jobs` row unconditionally — it never compares the replay's own `job_type`/`payload` against the original row's, so a caller that reuses a key for a genuinely *different* request silently receives the first request's job back instead of a rejection. This is the C-01 class ("idempotency-tuple gaps... claiming full tuple comparison but comparing only a leading subset," recurring at `PRC-257`/`258`/`259`, `PRC-261`/`262`/`263`) applied to a shared Platform primitive rather than a single domain RPC.

**Handling:** `PLT-132`'s own migration is already-applied and outside `CG-S11-PRC-017`'s allowed-files scope (a Phase-1 Platform capability, not a Phase-6 Procurement one) — fixing it upstream is a separate task with its own mandate and its own regression surface (every module that already calls `app.enqueue_job`: `COM-159`, `FIN-213`, `OPS-183`, and now `PRC-266`). `app.enqueue_procurement_report_export` performs its own real, full-tuple pre-check against `app.jobs` (`job_type`/`report_type_code`/`parameters`) before ever calling `app.enqueue_job`, raising `idempotency_key_conflict` on a genuine mismatch — this closes the gap for every caller reachable through this one new entry point, but does not fix `app.enqueue_job` itself, so any *other* future caller of `app.enqueue_job` that skips an equivalent pre-check remains exposed. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (mitigated at every currently-known call site's own layer; no live-reproduced cross-tenant or financial-integrity impact — a key collision only ever returns a caller's own already-enqueued job, never another tenant's) — re-attempt owner: whichever future task next touches `PLT-132`'s own migration file.

### ISS-2026-054 — C-05 tenant-id-disclosure oracle, widened to ≥10 more by-id RPCs across PRC-251/252/253/254/256 (RESOLVED, Medium)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S11-PRC-019` (Prompt 268, Procurement/Vendor Integrated Verification), by a live security-isolation sweep introspecting the full `get_/list_` by-id RPC surface (107 functions) via `pg_get_functiondef` against a live, fully-migrated database, independently re-derived by the Prompt 268 synthesis itself. `ISS-2026-043` (read RPCs) and `ISS-2026-048` (write RPCs) already register the pattern "a by-id RPC resolves the target row's real `tenant_id`, then echoes it verbatim into the `insufficient_authority` error text to a caller who has not yet been shown to belong to that tenant" — both entries enumerate specific fixed/still-open function lists. This sweep found the identical vulnerable shape, unfixed, in at least 10 further functions spanning PRC-251 (the phase's very first, unbatched, pre-`ADR-0021` capability), PRC-252, PRC-253, PRC-254, and PRC-256 — none of which appear in either issue's own enumerated disposition text: `app.suspend_vendor_profile` (and, by the identical code template, its lifecycle-transition siblings `reactivate_`/`archive_`/`blacklist_vendor_profile`), `app.get_vendor_assessment_score_breakdown`, `app.list_vendor_assessment_findings`, `app.list_vendor_assessment_template_criteria`, `app.list_vendor_assessment_corrective_actions`, `app.get_vendor_compliance_requirement`, `app.get_vendor_compliance_waiver`, `app.get_vendor_compliance_document`, `app.decide_vendor_compliance_waiver`, `app.get_vendor_payment_term_proposal`, `app.get_sourcing_request_history`, `app.list_sourcing_candidates`. Live-reproduced directly by the Prompt 268 synthesis for one instance (`app.get_vendor_compliance_requirement`): a fresh tenant + a real `vendor_compliance_requirements` row + an `auth.users` identity with ZERO `principal_memberships` rows anywhere, called with that identity's own session simulated — raised `insufficient_authority: identity 00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000c0502 lacks PRC:View (no_active_assignment) for tenant 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111`, disclosing the real tenant_id to a caller who is not a member of any tenant. The two write-path instances tested (`suspend_vendor_profile`, `decide_vendor_compliance_waiver`) correctly BLOCKED the actual state-changing action — only the tenant_id disclosure is the defect, not a privilege-escalation-to-write. `app.get_sourcing_request` itself remains the one already-disclosed, still-open `ISS-2026-043` instance, reconfirmed unchanged, not a new finding.

**Handling:** Not fixed by Prompt 268 (a documentation-only Integrated Verification checkpoint, `docs/build-log/phase-06/PRC-268.md` §6.2/§12: "this prompt does not fix defects, it finds and registers them"). The repair is the same already-established pattern `ISS-2026-043`/`048`'s own fixed instances use (fold the tenant-membership check into the not-found branch before disclosing any resolved `tenant_id`). **Status `OPEN`**, Medium severity (matches `ISS-2026-043`/`048`'s own severity — cross-tenant read/write access itself is correctly blocked in every case tested; only a low-value identifier is disclosed to a non-member) — owner: PRC-251/252/253/254/256's own owning capabilities, same repair pass that eventually closes `ISS-2026-043`/`048`'s remaining instances (Prompt 269, Hardening, is the next-eligible task with a mandate to fix Phase 6 findings).

**Resolved 2026-08-09 (`CG-S11-PRC-020`, Prompt 269 Hardening, `supabase/migrations/20260730820000_harden_procurement_c05_tenant_disclosure_sweep_batch5.sql`):** all 15 named functions fixed using the exact already-established pattern (`app.get_rfq`'s own template) — `app.has_active_tenant_membership(v_tenant_id, p_actor_auth_user_id)` folded into the SAME not-found branch the row-miss case already raised, so a non-member now gets the identical not-found error a genuinely missing id would produce, and only a real member ever reaches the real `evaluate_permission`/authority check below it. No permission check was weakened — the authority check itself is unchanged, only its ordering relative to the tenant-membership pre-check. `app.suspend_vendor_profile` also received `ISS-2026-055`'s own fix in the same `CREATE OR REPLACE` (see that entry). Regression evidence: one live-reproduced test per function (or per owning db-test file, matching each file's own established convention) added to `procurement-vendor-registration.sql`, `procurement-vendor-assessment.sql`, `procurement-vendor-compliance.sql`, `procurement-vendor-financial-security.sql`, and `procurement-sourcing.sql` — each proves a zero-membership identity calling the function against a real target row gets a not-found-shaped error, never the real `tenant_id`. `procurement-sourcing.sql`'s own two PRE-EXISTING cross-tenant assertions for `list_sourcing_candidates`/`get_sourcing_request_history` (which had asserted `insufficient_privilege`, the exact disclosing shape this fix closes) were updated to assert the new not-found shape instead — a deliberate, disclosed test-behavior change, not a weakened test. `app.get_sourcing_request` itself remains the one already-registered, still-open `ISS-2026-043` instance (out of this fix's own 15-function scope, tracked separately).

### ISS-2026-055 — `vendor_profiles` lifecycle-transition write path discloses `record_version` before the authority check (RESOLVED, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S11-PRC-019` (Prompt 268), by direct code inspection of `app.suspend_vendor_profile` (`supabase/migrations/20260730580000_create_procurement_vendor_registration.sql`) while investigating `ISS-2026-054` above, independently re-confirmed by the Prompt 268 synthesis reading the live function definition a second time. The function's `p_expected_version` check runs and can raise a `stale_version` error containing the row's real current `record_version` strictly BEFORE `app.evaluate_permission` is ever called — the same code template is shared by its lifecycle-transition siblings (`reactivate_`/`archive_`/`blacklist_vendor_profile`). A much lower-value oracle than `ISS-2026-054` (a numeric version counter, not a tenant/business-data value), and the same authorization-check-ordering class already disclosed at LOW severity for the Platform Approval Engine (`ISS-2026-049`, "entity_type discloses before authority check").

**Handling:** Not fixed by Prompt 268 (docs-only checkpoint). Fold the version check, like the tenant check (`ISS-2026-054`), behind or into the not-found/authority gate. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (a version counter disclosure, no tenant/business-data value, no privilege escalation) — owner: PRC-251, same hardening pass as `ISS-2026-054`.

**Resolved 2026-08-09 (`CG-S11-PRC-020`, Prompt 269 Hardening, `supabase/migrations/20260730820000_harden_procurement_c05_tenant_disclosure_sweep_batch5.sql`):** each of `app.suspend_vendor_profile`/`reactivate_vendor_profile`/`archive_vendor_profile`/`blacklist_vendor_profile` was individually read (a structural sweep, not a blind grep-and-copy) and confirmed to share the identical ordering bug — all four reordered to fetch the row (folded into `ISS-2026-054`'s own not-found branch) → evaluate the authority check → THEN the `stale_version` check, so neither the real `tenant_id` nor the real `record_version` is ever disclosed to a caller not yet shown to hold both tenant membership and the required permission. Regression evidence: `scripts/db-tests/procurement-vendor-registration.sql` gained one new test block proving, for all four functions, both (1) the cross-tenant not-found shape (`ISS-2026-054`) and (2) a real tenant member who both lacks the required authority and supplies a deliberately stale `expected_version` gets `insufficient_authority`, never `stale_version` — confirming the new ordering, plus a sanity check that the fixture vendor's `lifecycle_status`/`record_version` are genuinely untouched by every rejected call.

**Correction, same checkpoint (2026-08-09, `CG-S11-PRC-020` Prompt 269 Hardening's own adversarial security-regression review round, before this checkpoint's own two new migrations were ever committed):** the resolution paragraph directly above, and this same checkpoint's own build log (`docs/build-log/phase-06/PRC-269.md` §2 Fix 5), both originally stated that `app.decide_vendor_compliance_waiver` was individually checked and confirmed to NOT share this ordering defect ("its own `self_approval_not_allowed` identity check runs before `stale_version` on identity grounds"). A live re-check against the actual applied function body (`pg_get_functiondef`), prompted by this same round's own instruction to spot-check any "checked and found NOT affected" claim, found that statement FALSE: `stale_version` ran BEFORE both `self_approval_not_allowed` and the `PRC:Approve`/`PRC:Reject` authority check in the function's real body, so a real tenant member holding neither authority (and not the waiver's own requester) could still extract the waiver's genuine current `record_version` via a deliberately stale `p_expected_version`, before ever being told they lacked authority to decide it. Live-reproduced: `viewer@pcmp1.test` (real `PRC:View`-only tenant member, `PRC:Approve=false`, `PRC:Reject=false`, confirmed via `evaluate_permission`) calling `app.decide_vendor_compliance_waiver` with a real waiver id and a wrong `p_expected_version` received `stale_version: ... expected version 999 but found 3` — the row's real version — instead of `insufficient_authority`. Not a full authorization bypass (re-checked separately with the correct version: the same actor is still correctly denied `insufficient_authority`) — a disclosure-ordering defect only, matching this issue's own severity and shape. **Fixed in place, same migration, before commit** (`supabase/migrations/20260730820000_harden_procurement_c05_tenant_disclosure_sweep_batch5.sql`, this checkpoint's own not-yet-committed file — edited directly rather than stacked with a further migration, per this checkpoint's own applied-migration discipline): `app.decide_vendor_compliance_waiver` now runs `self_approval_not_allowed` and the authority check (their own prior relative order to each other unchanged) BEFORE `stale_version`/`invalid_transition`, matching the same "authority before state-disclosure" ordering as the four `vendor_profiles` functions above. Regression evidence: `scripts/db-tests/procurement-vendor-compliance.sql` gained two new assertions (a non-requester lacking authority, and the requester itself, each supplying a deliberately stale `expected_version`) proving `insufficient_authority`/`self_approval_not_allowed` fire, never `stale_version`, plus a sanity check that the fixture waiver's real `record_version`/`status` are untouched by any of the rejected calls.

### ISS-2026-056 — `app.list_vendor_contracts` missing `(tenant_id, created_at desc)` covering index (RESOLVED, Medium)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S11-PRC-019` (Prompt 268), by a live performance/migration sweep, independently re-confirmed by the Prompt 268 synthesis via a direct `pg_indexes` query against a live, fully-migrated database. `app.vendor_contracts` (`supabase/migrations/20260730700000_create_procurement_vendor_contract.sql`, PRC-261) carries indexes on `(tenant_id, contract_number, version_no)` ×2, `(tenant_id, effective_end)` partial, and `(tenant_id, vendor_master_id, status)` — but none on `(tenant_id, created_at desc)`. Its three sibling list-instrument RPCs in the same PRC-25x/26x family all carry the matching index, independently confirmed present: `rfqs_tenant_created_idx` (`app.rfqs`), `purchase_orders_tenant_created_idx` (`app.purchase_orders`), `vendor_comparisons_tenant_created_idx` (`app.vendor_comparisons`). `app.list_vendor_contracts`'s own internal query (`select * from app.vendor_contracts where tenant_id = p_tenant_id ... order by created_at desc limit ...`) is the identical shape to its siblings' own internal queries, but lacking the matching index the planner cannot do an ordered Index Scan with early-LIMIT termination the way `app.list_purchase_orders` does. At a realistic proportional 25-tenant/~500-contract-per-tenant scale (12,500 rows total, ~4% per-tenant selectivity) it still correctly uses a tenant-scoped Bitmap Index Scan (via the `(tenant_id, vendor_master_id, status)` index's leading column) and does not degrade to a full Seq Scan; under a live-reproduced single-tenant-concentration test (one tenant holding 68% of the table), the identical query degrades to a full Seq Scan on `app.vendor_contracts`. A CargoGrid tenant with a genuinely large individual contract count would see this RPC's latency scale linearly with its own row count rather than the O(log n + limit) behavior its three siblings already have.

**Handling:** Not fixed by Prompt 268 (§13: "prefer no production schema change" — a docs-only Integrated Verification checkpoint is not the place for a new index migration). Add a `(tenant_id, created_at desc)` index on `app.vendor_contracts`, mirroring the three sibling tables exactly. **Status `OPEN`**, Medium severity (no seq scan yet at realistic proportional scale; a real, reproducible degradation under single-tenant concentration, which a large enterprise customer could plausibly reach) — owner: PRC-261, a future schema-touching hardening task (Prompt 269).

**Resolved 2026-08-09 (`CG-S11-PRC-020`, Prompt 269 Hardening, `supabase/migrations/20260730820000_harden_procurement_c05_tenant_disclosure_sweep_batch5.sql`):** `create index vendor_contracts_tenant_created_idx on app.vendor_contracts (tenant_id, created_at desc);` — plain `CREATE INDEX`, mirroring the three sibling tables' naming exactly (no `CONCURRENTLY` anywhere in this repository's own migrations, confirmed by grep). Verified live against a seeded, skewed dataset mirroring this entry's own reproduction (7,497 total rows, one tenant holding 5,100 = 68.0%): `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` against `app.list_vendor_contracts`'s own exact query shape went from `Seq Scan on vendor_contracts` (203 buffer hits, 3.03ms) with the index absent to `Index Scan using vendor_contracts_tenant_created_idx` (3 buffer hits, 0.09ms) with it present — confirmed via a throwaway database, never wired into the permanent `db:test` suite (a multi-thousand-row seed does not belong in the standing regression gate).

### ISS-2026-059 — `app._calc_vendor_kpi_rate_validity` (PRC-264) fails `procurement-vendor-performance.sql` deterministically when run between ~00:00–03:59 UTC (OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S11-PRC-020` (Prompt 269 Hardening)'s own adversarial review round, closing out three independent review lenses (financial-currency-correctness, security-regression, full-regression-and-integration) — all three independently hit the identical `pnpm run db:test` failure (`scripts/db-tests/procurement-vendor-performance.sql:978`, `assertion failed: expected New Vendor rate_validity to be computable (a real 0%, not a missing-data case)`) and all three correctly confirmed, via `git stash`/baseline re-runs, that it reproduces identically against the pre-PRC-269 baseline — i.e. genuinely pre-existing, not caused by any of this checkpoint's own changes. None of the three lenses root-caused it beyond "pre-existing, unrelated" (out of each lens's own assigned scope); this checkpoint's own fix round did, while reproducing the finding, and records the real mechanism here rather than leaving only a prose disclosure with no ledger entry (the specific gap the full-regression lens itself flagged as CONFIRMED — no `ISS-2026-0NN` tracking existed for this failure despite every other deferred gap in this checkpoint having one).

**Root cause, live-verified, not assumed:** `app._calc_vendor_kpi_rate_validity` (`supabase/migrations/20260730740000_create_procurement_vendor_performance.sql:1186`) computes its own calendar-day denominator via `generate_series(p_window_start::date, (p_window_end - interval '1 day')::date, interval '1 day')`. For the test's own fixed 21-hour window (`v_window_start := date_trunc('hour', now()) - interval '1 hour'`, `v_window_end := v_window_start + interval '21 hours'`), the upper bound simplifies to `(p_window_start - interval '3 hours')::date` — which falls on the PREVIOUS calendar date relative to `p_window_start::date` whenever `p_window_start`'s own hour-of-day is less than 3 (UTC, this sandbox's server timezone). When that happens, `generate_series` is called with a start date AFTER its end date, which PostgreSQL correctly returns as zero rows (ascending step, descending bound) — collapsing `v_den` (and therefore `sample_size`) to `0`, which flips `is_computable` to `false` even though the window itself is real, non-empty, and (per this function's own comment) meant to be unconditionally computable. Live-reproduced directly, isolated from the rest of the test file: at `now() = 2026-08-09 02:38:31 UTC`, `(date_trunc('hour', now()) - interval '1 hour')::date = 2026-08-09` but `((date_trunc('hour', now()) + interval '20 hours') - interval '1 day')::date = 2026-08-08` — start-date > end-date, `generate_series(...)` returns 0 rows, confirmed via direct `select count(*) from generate_series(...)`. This is a genuine, deterministic, time-of-day-dependent off-by-one in the function's own day-window boundary arithmetic, not a flaky/nondeterministic test — it fails on every run whose wall-clock time falls in roughly the `00:00`–`03:59 UTC` band (as this checkpoint's own sandbox time did throughout this review round, explaining why all three lenses, and this checkpoint's own re-runs, hit it consistently) and passes cleanly outside that band (confirmed: every prior checkpoint's own build log, including `PRC-269`'s own original §7, reported this file passing).

**Handling:** Not fixed by this checkpoint. `app._calc_vendor_kpi_rate_validity` lives in `PRC-264`'s own migration (`20260730740000_create_procurement_vendor_performance.sql`), a different capability/checkpoint than the six findings `CG-S11-PRC-020` (Prompt 269) was chartered to fix, and this checkpoint's own adversarial-review mandate is to close the three lenses' CONFIRMED findings against Prompt 269's own fix pass, not to open and fix an unrelated capability's pre-existing defect discovered incidentally — the same scope-discipline reasoning `docs/build-log/phase-06/PRC-269.md` §6 already applied when it first disclosed this failure in prose without registering it. The eventual fix is bounded and low-risk once undertaken: replace the `(p_window_end - interval '1 day')::date` upper bound with an inclusive-end computation that does not depend on time-of-day sign (e.g. `(p_window_end - interval '1 second')::date`, or deriving the day count directly via `date(p_window_end) - date(p_window_start)` with an explicit floor/ceiling decision on partial trailing days) — a `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` against this same function, plus a regression test that pins the window to specific UTC hours (e.g. `01:00`–`22:00` AND `10:00`–`11:00`) rather than a `now()`-relative window whose pass/fail depends on when the suite happens to run. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (self-heals outside the ~4-hour daily UTC band; no data-integrity impact — the metric value that would be recomputed with the wrong `is_computable` is never published as a scorecard line in a way that silently fabricates a value, since `is_computable=false` correctly still routes the vendor into `insufficient_kpi_coverage`/reduced-coverage handling rather than showing a wrong number) — but a real, currently-red `db:test` gate for roughly one-sixth of any given day; owner: PRC-264, a future task with an explicit mandate to touch `20260730740000`'s own capability.

**Handling:** Not fixed by this checkpoint (disclosed scope trim under time/size constraints for a single capability checkpoint, per Prompt 274 §28's own "if you have time, add [E2E]; if not, disclose it as a residual gap" instruction) — the staged-import TS wrapper gap named in the correction above WAS fixed in the same review-round fix pass. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (UI-depth gaps over an already-real, already-tested service layer, no security/data-integrity exposure) — owner: HRT-274 follow-up or a later Phase 7 UI-hardening checkpoint (HRT-293/295 are the phase's own dedicated privacy/integrity-hardening slots and are the natural place to close this before Phase 7 closure).

### ISS-2026-065 — Employee Master (HRT-274): no effective-dated employee identity/lifecycle mechanism, despite a binding, repeated Prompt 274 requirement (OPEN, High)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during the same-checkpoint (`CG-S12-HRT-002`, Prompt 274, Employee Master) adversarial review round (correctness/concurrency lens), independently re-derived by the fix pass before being accepted. `274_EMPLOYEE_MASTER_PROMPT.md` names "effective dates"/"effective-dated"/"effective version" as a required, non-optional element in multiple sections: §5 ("one effective-dated workforce truth"), §13 (fields this checkpoint must extend the domain with), §17 (indexing "... effective period"), §18 (audit records must include "effective version"), §20 ("Define effective-dated employee identity, lifecycle, duplicate and correction invariants"). ADR-0023 Part B's own invariant language ("one employee workforce profile may link to zero or one active Platform user identity PER EFFECTIVE CONTEXT") is time-boxed phrasing a permanent, unconditional partial-unique-index (`employees_user_id_unique`) structurally cannot represent. The original migration's own decision note (`supabase/migrations/20260730830000_create_hris_employee_master.sql`) claimed this requirement was satisfied because `app.master_records` already carries `effective_from`/`effective_to` — live `grep` across the full migration found those two columns referenced nowhere outside that one comment: no function in the migration reads or writes them for any employee purpose, `app.employees` itself has no effective-dated column of its own (only simple point-in-time `hire_date`/`probation_end_date`/`employment_end_date`), and no write RPC (`create_employee_draft`, `update_employee_draft`, `transfer_employee`, or any lifecycle transition) accepts an effective-date parameter or supports scheduling, backdating, or an "as of" query. Every change takes effect immediately at `now()`.

**Handling:** The false claim itself is corrected in place (the migration's own header comment, `docs/build-log/phase-07/HRT-274.md` §3.1/§11, `docs/build-log/phase-07/00_EXECUTION_INDEX.md`, `docs/runtime/CARGOGRID_BUILD_STATUS.md`, and `docs/runtime/TASK_LEDGER.md` all now accurately describe the lifecycle as point-in-time, not effective-dated), but a genuine effective-dating mechanism (real temporal/bi-temporal columns, "as of" query semantics across every lifecycle RPC and read projection) is a materially new capability — judged architecturally out of scope for a bounded review-round fix, and force-building it without the same depth of proof this checkpoint gave everything else would risk shipping a new, unverified defect class rather than closing one. **Status `OPEN`**, High severity (a named, repeated, binding requirement is genuinely unimplemented, though no security/tenant-isolation exposure exists — every RPC that IS implemented correctly enforces authority/concurrency/masking regardless of this gap) — owner: a future HRT task, before `HRT-293` (Sensitive personal and payroll data controls) or `HRT-294` (Integrated verification), since both depend on this capability's data model being materially final.

**Update (`2026-08-09`, `CG-S12-HRT-003`, Prompt 275, Organization and Position Linkage):** HRT-275 delivers a genuinely effective-dated mechanism for one specific, real slice of this gap — `app.employee_position_assignments` (`supabase/migrations/20260730840000_create_hris_organization_position_linkage.sql`) is a real, new, effective-dated (`effective_start_date`/`effective_end_date`, a `validity_range` generated column, an `app.get_employee_current_assignment(p_as_of date)` point-in-time read) history table for an employee's position/grade/manager assignment specifically, satisfying Prompt 275's own §13 "effective range"/§20 "historical queries" requirement in full for that domain. **This does NOT close `ISS-2026-065`** — the two are different claims. `ISS-2026-065` is about the EMPLOYEE's own record (`lifecycle_status`, `hire_date`, `probation_end_date`, `employment_end_date`, and every HRT-274 lifecycle-transition RPC), none of which HRT-275 touches or effective-dates; `app.employees.lifecycle_status` still transitions immediately at `now()` with no scheduling/backdating/"as of" capability, exactly as this entry originally found. Disclosed here explicitly so a future reader does not conflate "HRT-275 shipped effective-dated assignments" with "the employee lifecycle gap is closed" — it is not. `ISS-2026-065` remains `OPEN`, High, with the same owner/timing as originally recorded.

**Update (`2026-08-15`, dedicated HRT follow-up task, HRT-ISS-065-CLOSURE):** the Prompt 297 closure checkpoint (`CG-S12-HRT-025`) independently re-confirmed this entry CONFIRMED STILL OPEN and named it the sole remaining blocker to `PHASE_7_VERIFIED` (`docs/build-log/phase-07/HRIS_TICKETING_CLOSURE_REPORT.md` §19/§20/§22), and its own §22 named the exact resume condition: "a dedicated HRT follow-up prompt... Design and implement a genuine effective-dated (or bi-temporal) identity/lifecycle mechanism for `app.employees`." The operator explicitly authorized this dedicated follow-up task to build it as bounded new capability work. **Status `RESOLVED`.** `supabase/migrations/20260731310000_add_hris_employee_lifecycle_effective_dating_iss2026065.sql` adds `app.employee_lifecycle_versions` — a real, versioned, effective-dated history table for the employee's own record (`lifecycle_status`, company/branch/department/position/manager, `employment_type`, `hire_date`/`probation_end_date`/`employment_end_date`), mirroring `app.employee_position_assignments`' own shape (`effective_start_date`/`effective_end_date`, a generated `validity_range`, `status`, `change_reason`, `previous_version_id` chain, `decided_by`/`decided_at`/`decided_reason`, `record_version`). Every one of the 7 lifecycle-transition RPCs named by the original finding (`create_employee_draft`, `update_employee_draft`, `transfer_employee`, `suspend_employee`, `terminate_employee`, `reactivate_employee`, `archive_employee_profile`) now accepts an optional `p_effective_date` (defaulting to `current_date`, fully backward-compatible — verified against every existing positional and named-parameter call site in this repository without editing any of them), with a genuine future-scheduled path (deferred to a new maintenance sweep, `app.activate_due_employee_lifecycle_transitions`, HRS:Override-gated/idempotent/`NOT_RUN` — no live scheduler exists anywhere in this repository, the same standing, disclosed `ISS-2026-015` gap) and a genuine backdated-correction path (gated at least as strictly as `HRS:Override`, a mandatory reason, and a supersede-before-insert reconciliation of any intervening history). `app.get_employee_lifecycle_as_of(p_master_record_id, p_actor_auth_user_id, p_as_of)` is the real "as of" read this entry's own §17/§18/§20 citations required, mirroring `app.get_employee_current_assignment`'s own shape — reconstructs genuine historical/current/future state directly from `app.employee_lifecycle_versions`, never from `app.employees`' own current-state columns. Composition with HRT-295's already-VERIFIED identity coupling (`app.transition_user_status`) is timing-correct in both directions, live-tested: an immediate/backdated transition couples in the same transaction exactly as HRT-295 established (byte-identical statements, unmodified); a future-scheduled transition defers the Platform-identity call until the sweep genuinely activates it, never earlier (no premature revocation) and never omitted (no regression of the HRT-295 security fix). Every existing downstream reader of `app.employees.lifecycle_status` (attendance/leave/overtime/payroll eligibility checks) was grepped and confirmed unmodified and correct as-is — additive, not breaking. Full regression + new-capability proof in `scripts/db-tests/hris-employee-master-lifecycle-effective-dating.sql` (a dedicated new file) plus a required signature-reference fix to `scripts/db-tests/hris-employee-master.sql`'s own pre-existing schema-privilege defense-in-depth test (the 7 RPCs' argument-type signatures genuinely changed — `DROP FUNCTION`+`CREATE FUNCTION`, since `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` cannot add a parameter). Full detail, design decisions, Tier B taxonomy self-check, and gate results: `docs/build-log/phase-07/HRT-ISS-065-CLOSURE.md`.

### ISS-2026-066 — Organization and Position Linkage (HRT-275): no bulk/multi-employee reorganization wizard, no live scheduler for future-dated assignment activation, no staged-import crosswalk for position/grade, and no browser/accessibility E2E (OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S12-HRT-003` (Prompt 275, Organization and Position Linkage), by this checkpoint's own scope-completeness self-check before closing, mirroring HRT-274's own `ISS-2026-064` disclosure discipline. The full domain/service layer for every item below is real, tested, and live — what is disclosed here is UI/automation depth beyond it, not a broken or fabricated code path:

1. **No bulk/multi-employee reorganization wizard.** Every RPC (`app.propose_employee_position_assignment`, `app.decide_employee_position_assignment`, `app.cancel_employee_position_assignment`) and the UI wizard at `/hris/employees/[masterRecordId]/positions` operate one employee at a time. A "move an entire department's employees to a new org unit/position in one transaction" tool is a genuinely new capability, not a bounded extension of this checkpoint's own singular-employee-centric table (section 13's own "employee-assignment/version table" wording).
2. **No live cron/scheduler invokes `app.activate_due_employee_position_assignments` automatically.** The RPC is real, HRS:Override-gated, idempotent, and proven live in `scripts/db-tests/hris-organization-position-linkage.sql`'s own "maintenance sweep" block — but nothing in this repository calls it on a schedule yet (no `pg_cron` or equivalent scheduler exists anywhere in this repository, the same standing gap `ISS-2026-015` already discloses repository-wide). Until it is invoked (by hand, by a future job scheduler, or by a Server Action a human triggers), a future-dated, approved assignment's `app.employees.position_id`/`manager_employee_id` convenience-cache columns remain stale past their own `effective_start_date` until the sweep runs — `app.get_employee_current_assignment`'s own `p_as_of` read is unaffected (it reads `app.employee_position_assignments` directly, never the cache) and is always correct regardless.
3. **No staged-import (PLT-131/132) crosswalk for position/grade/assignment rows.** Section 19's own "map existing department/position strings to canonical IDs through staged, reviewed crosswalks" describes a bulk-migration capability this checkpoint deliberately did not build (disclosed in the migration's own header, decision 10) — building a first-of-its-kind crosswalk-import UI was judged disproportionate, unrequested scope for this checkpoint.
4. **No Playwright/axe-core E2E spec** exists yet for the position catalogue, organization tree, or assignment-timeline/wizard pages — matching HRT-274's own `ISS-2026-064` item (3) precedent, not yet followed here either.

None of the four blocks HR staff from using the shipped capability (position/grade CRUD, organization-linked position tree, propose/approve/reject/cancel assignment workflow with impact preview, effective-dated point-in-time reads, hierarchy reads) — all real, RLS/RBAC-enforced, and exercised by `scripts/db-tests/hris-organization-position-linkage.sql`.

**Handling:** Not fixed by this checkpoint (disclosed scope trim under time/size constraints for a single capability checkpoint, mirroring `ISS-2026-064`'s own identical disposition). **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (UI/automation-depth gaps over an already-real, already-tested service layer; no security/data-integrity exposure — item 2's staleness window is a disclosed, bounded read-freshness gap, not a correctness defect, since `app.get_employee_current_assignment` is always accurate) — owner: a later Phase 7 UI-hardening checkpoint (HRT-293/294/295, the phase's own dedicated hardening/verification slots) or a dedicated future scheduler-infrastructure task for item 2 specifically.

### ISS-2026-067 — Recruitment, Job Portal and ATS (HRT-276): no UI caller yet for duplicate-review, exports, assessment/interview cancel-shaped actions, and no standalone candidate directory (OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-09` during `CG-S12-HRT-004` (Prompt 276, Recruitment, Job Portal and ATS), by this checkpoint's own Tier B taxonomy self-check (class C-20) before closing, mirroring `ISS-2026-064`/`ISS-2026-066`'s own disclosure discipline. The full domain/service layer for every item below is real, tested, and live — what is disclosed here is UI depth beyond it, not a broken or fabricated code path:
