Here, no customer-facing inbound-order RPC exists ANYWHERE in this repository, before or after this migration — grep-confirmed zero `app.get_customer_inbound_order`/`app.list_customer_inbound_orders` in `supabase/migrations/`. `app.wms_inbound_orders` (ATW-012, `supabase/migrations/20260730180000_create_advanced_tms_wms_inbound.sql:108-137`) does carry both `warehouse_id` and `owner_account_id` — the identical shape `app.evaluate_customer_portal_inventory_access` (CPL-309) already expects and this checkpoint's own three RPCs already reuse unmodified — so a symmetrical inbound-order customer surface is technically straightforward future work, not a structural impossibility; it was simply never built by ATW-023 (Phase 5) or any later checkpoint, and this task's own explicit design section named exactly three RPCs to build, all outbound, matching ATW-023's own real, already-shipped scope.

**Live effect:** a customer_portal user viewing `/customer-warehouse-orders` today sees every OUTBOUND order WMS is fulfilling for their own accounts (correctly scoped, correctly ISS-2026-117-fixed), but sees nothing about inbound/receiving activity for those same accounts — not because of a scope bug, but because no RPC exists to query it. The UI never claims otherwise: every order row is honestly labeled "Outbound" (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/customer-warehouse-orders/customer-warehouse-orders-panel.tsx`), never a fabricated inbound row with no backing data. Not a security issue and not a live caller regression — grep-confirmed zero caller anywhere in `server/`/`app/` expects an inbound-order projection from this capability.

**Not fixed here** — this checkpoint's own explicit file/migration budget (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations) and its own chartered scope (the source prompt's own design section naming exactly three outbound RPCs to mirror) intentionally stopped there. Designing a wholly new inbound-order customer RPC surface from scratch — gate composition (already reusable unmodified), column projection, anti-enumeration, cursor pagination, and its own live db-test regression proof — is a capability-sized addition in its own right, not a bounded extension of this checkpoint. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (no live caller depends on the deferred surface; the UI never claims inbound visibility it does not have). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks it up: a new additive migration mirroring this checkpoint's own three functions' shape for `app.wms_inbound_orders`/`app.wms_inbound_order_lines`, reusing `app.evaluate_customer_portal_inventory_access`/`app.resolve_customer_account_scope` unchanged, plus a live db-test regression proof mirroring this checkpoint's own key isolation/anti-enumeration/pagination assertions.

### ISS-2026-121 — "finance scope" is the same undifferentiated Layer 4 account scope every other Phase 8 domain already uses -- no per-domain sub-permission exists to narrow it further (Phase 8, CPL-311 deliberate scope decision, OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-013` (Prompt 311, Invoice and Billing Visibility) — a deliberate scope decision made while authoring this checkpoint's own migration, not a defect found afterward. The source prompt's own text explicitly required this checkpoint to "confirm this by checking CPL-300's own membership/role model before finalizing this decision," which is what this entry records.

**Code:** `app.evaluate_customer_portal_invoice_access` (`supabase/migrations/20260801120000_create_customer_portal_invoice_billing_visibility.sql`) is `p_customer_account_id = any(app.resolve_customer_account_scope(p_auth_user_id, p_tenant_id))` — deliberately simpler than CPL-309's `app.evaluate_customer_portal_inventory_access`, which composes a SECOND real predicate (`app.customer_warehouse_eligibility_active`, backed by a genuine `app.warehouse_customer_eligibility` table). Checked directly before writing this gate, not assumed: `app.customer_portal_account_memberships` (CPL-300, `supabase/migrations/20260801010000_create_customer_portal_account_scope.sql:126-149`) carries exactly one role column, CHECK-constrained to `account_admin`/`member` — no module/domain sub-scope of any kind. `app.accounts` (`20260724290000_create_commercial_customer_account_conversion.sql`) itself carries no per-domain visibility flag either. There is therefore no data anywhere in this repository today that could back a narrower "finance scope" than plain account scope, for either role.

**Live effect:** a `member`-role customer_portal user granted access to an account for one purpose (e.g. viewing that account's warehouse orders, per CPL-310) automatically also sees that same account's own invoices through this checkpoint's own new RPCs, with no separate finance-specific grant required. This is NOT a new widening CPL-311 introduces on its own: the identical account-scope-alone boundary already governs every other Phase 8 domain capability shipped so far (CPL-303's booking requests, CPL-304's shipment orders, CPL-309's inventory balances, CPL-310's warehouse orders — none of them layer a domain-specific sub-permission on top of account scope either). CPL-311 is simply the first checkpoint where this shared, pre-existing granularity becomes visible for Finance data specifically, since Finance data (amounts, payment status) is more commonly treated as sensitive within an organization than warehouse/shipment status.

**Not fixed here** — inventing a new per-domain sub-permission column or table (e.g. a `finance_scope` flag on `app.customer_portal_account_memberships`, or a wholly separate Finance-specific delegation grant table) is a genuinely new, capability-sized data-model decision, out of this prompt's own bounded scope (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations) and out of scope for a single capability prompt to invent unilaterally per `BUILD_EXECUTION_PROTOCOL.md`'s own discipline. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (matches every other already-`VERIFIED` Phase 8 capability's own identical account-scope granularity; no data is fabricated, no existing caller is affected, and the business rule this prompt names — "invoice visibility requires customer finance scope, not generic shipment access alone" — is satisfied literally: finance scope IS the account scope, since no narrower concept exists to satisfy it with). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks it up, if the business ever requires narrower in-account granularity: a new, additive per-module delegation mechanism, composed by ALL Phase 8 domain gates uniformly (not just Finance), to avoid Finance alone gaining an inconsistent, narrower shape than its siblings.

### ISS-2026-122 — the new warehouse_order/document ticket-link surface is a genuinely separate table from app.ticket_links, document has no staff predicate yet, pre-creation search has no per-attempt audit ledger, and the three PRE-EXISTING app.ticket_links entity types remain on the legacy scope resolver (Phase 8, CPL-313 deliberate scope decisions, OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-015` (Prompt 313, Complaint and Ticket) — four deliberate scope decisions made while authoring this checkpoint's own migration, not defects found afterward. Item 4 below was added `2026-08-17` at this same batch's own Tier C review close, correcting this checkpoint's own migration header (design decision 5) and build log (`docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-313.md` §2 decision 6), both of which cited this entry as already recording the item before it had actually been written in here — a real citation-accuracy gap the spec-compliance review lens caught; the underlying design decision itself was genuine and correctly disclosed at authoring time, only the citation's target was incomplete.

**Item 1 — a parallel table, not a widened registry, and why.** The source prompt's own research suggested widening `app.ticket_links.entity_type`'s CHECK constraint (the sanctioned HRT-275-style DROP+ADD non-destructive widening) to add `warehouse_order`/`document` alongside the existing six values. Direct inspection BEFORE writing any code — per the source prompt's own explicit instruction to check `app._ticket_link_resolve_candidate`'s actual body first — found this path foreclosed by two real, already-applied, protected test assertions: `scripts/db-tests/ticketing-linked-records.sql:254` (`if v_full <> array['shipment','invoice','warehouse','vendor','customer','user']::text[] then raise exception 'FAIL: ... drifted from the documented six-value registry'`) and `server/contracts/ticketing/ticketing.test.ts:630` (`assert.deepEqual([...TICKET_LINK_ENTITY_TYPES].sort(), [...six values])`). Both are existing, already-passing tests this task's own instructions forbid deleting or modifying, and widening the shared registry would make both fail — a real regression, not a cosmetic one. This checkpoint's own migration (`supabase/migrations/20260801140000_create_customer_portal_ticket_linked_records.sql`) therefore leaves `app.ticket_links`/`app.ticket_link_events`/`app.ticket_link_entity_types()`/`app.ticket_link_customer_safe_entity_types()`/`app._ticket_link_resolve_candidate`/`app.search_ticket_link_candidates`/`app.link_ticket_record`/`app.unlink_ticket_record`/`app.list_ticket_links` completely untouched (grep-confirmed zero `alter table`/`create or replace function` against any of them) and instead adds a genuinely new, small, parallel `app.ticket_portal_links` table + RPC family, scoped to exactly the two new entity types. The customer-facing UI and the ticket creation picker present this as ONE unified search (`app.search_customer_ticket_link_candidates_precreate` spans both registries in one call), so the split is invisible to the customer; it is visible only in the schema and the service layer (`server/queries/ticketing.ts`/`server/mutations/ticketing.ts` carry a second, parallel set of `*TicketPortalLink*` functions).

**Item 2 — `document` is customer-portal-only.** `app._ticket_portal_link_resolve_candidate`'s `document` branch has no staff OR-branch, because no staff-facing document-browse/access predicate exists anywhere in this repository (CPL-308's own already-disclosed boundary, `docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-308.md` §2 design decision 4: "Neither `app.check_file_action_authority` nor `app.authorize_file_access` is composed"). A staff caller selecting `document` in a future internal-ticket-linking UI (none exists today — `TICKET_LINK_ENTITY_TYPES`, the registry the internal `tickets/[ticketId]` workspace's own picker reads, is unchanged by this checkpoint and never includes `document`) would see zero candidates, always — safe deny-by-default, not a leak, but also not yet a real staff capability.

**Item 3 — pre-creation search has no audit-ledger entry.** `app.ticket_link_events.ticket_id` is `NOT NULL` by design (HRT-292), and this checkpoint deliberately does not touch that table or invent a second ledger of its own (`app.ticket_portal_links`' own `created_by`/`removed_by`/`removed_reason`/timestamps/`record_version` already carry real, queryable history for every actual link/unlink once a ticket exists). The one genuine gap: a pre-creation SEARCH (before any ticket exists, via `app.search_customer_ticket_link_candidates_precreate`) has nowhere to durably log a denial, since no `ticket_id` exists yet to scope a ledger row to — low-risk, since the search itself is deny-by-default and returns nothing an unauthorized caller could act on, and the ACTUAL link attempt (once the ticket exists) is captured normally.

**Item 4 — the three PRE-EXISTING `app.ticket_links` entity types (`shipment`/`invoice`/`warehouse`) remain on the legacy `app.resolve_customer_owner_account_scope`, never CPL-300's widened `app.resolve_customer_account_scope`.** This checkpoint's own two NEW entity types (`warehouse_order`/`document`) consistently use the widened CPL-300 resolver in every function this checkpoint adds (`app._ticket_portal_link_resolve_candidate`, both search variants) — disclosed in the migration's own design decision 5 — but the three entity types `app.ticket_links` (HRT-292, Phase 7, already `VERIFIED`) already supported before this checkpoint are unaffected by anything this checkpoint builds, and stay on the resolver they always used. Matches the identical under-scoping SHAPE `ISS-2026-119`/CPL-311's own design decision 13 already name for other Phase 8 surfaces (a `customer_user` granted a second account ONLY through CPL-300's new grant table, never the legacy `customer_account_ref` marker, would not see that account's shipment/invoice/warehouse candidates through `app.search_ticket_link_candidates`/`app.link_ticket_record`, even though the SAME account's warehouse_order/document candidates ARE correctly visible through this checkpoint's own new functions). Not a leak (never an over-scoping issue) and not something this checkpoint introduced — `app.ticket_links` is an already-applied HRT-292 migration this checkpoint does not own and may not edit in place.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 is a discovered necessity (breaking a protected, already-passing test is not an acceptable trade for a widening path that was only ever "if genuinely needed"); item 2 mirrors CPL-308's own already-accepted, disclosed boundary rather than inventing a new staff-access predicate outside this checkpoint's own bounded scope; item 3 is structural to the existing `app.ticket_link_events` schema (`NOT NULL ticket_id`), not a gap this checkpoint introduced arbitrarily; item 4 is a pre-existing HRT-292 resolver-granularity gap, not something this checkpoint's own new code causes or can fix in place (editing `20260731170000_create_ticket_linked_records.sql` is forbidden) — closing it for `shipment`/`invoice`/`warehouse` would require its own additive `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` migration mirroring `ISS-2026-119`'s own recommended fix shape, out of this checkpoint's own bounded scope. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all four (no data fabricated, no existing HRT-292 caller/test affected, every new candidate independently reauthorized at both search time and actual link time; item 4 is under- not over-scoping). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks these up: item 2 — compose a real staff document-access predicate once one exists, mirroring how `warehouse_order`'s own staff branch already composes `app.wms_pick_record_scope_ok`/`app.actor_can_view_owner_scoped_row`; item 1 — no fix needed unless a future, unrelated reason to widen the original six-value registry arises, at which point the split could be reconciled in one additive migration; item 4 — a new additive migration `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`-ing `app._ticket_link_resolve_candidate`/`app.search_ticket_link_candidates` (HRT-292) to compose `app.resolve_customer_account_scope` instead of the legacy resolver for the `shipment`/`invoice`/`warehouse` customer-owner branches, mirroring `ISS-2026-119`'s own recommended fix and this same batch's own `20260801160000_harden_customer_portal_ticket_link_invoice_status_gate.sql` precedent for touching those two functions safely.

### ISS-2026-123 — legal_name/tax_id are excluded from the customer-writable field set, and contacts are read-only with no change-request path (Phase 8, CPL-314 deliberate scope decisions, OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-016` (Prompt 314, Customer Profile) — two deliberate scope decisions made while authoring this checkpoint's own migration, not defects found afterward. The source prompt's own text requires exactly this kind of disclosed call: "Billing, tax/legal and credit fields require configured authorization/approval," which this checkpoint reads as excluding legal identity fields from self-service change entirely (no configured authorization/approval workflow for a legal-name/tax-id change exists anywhere in this repository, and building one — likely involving real KYC/compliance review, not merely a staff click-to-approve — is a genuinely new, capability-sized addition, not a bounded extension of this prompt's own charter).

**Item 1 — `app.customer_portal_profile_change_requests.field_name` is CHECK-constrained to exactly `trade_name`/`billing_address`.** `app.accounts` (COM-155, `20260724290000_create_commercial_customer_account_conversion.sql`) carries `legal_name`/`tax_id` as real, mutable columns, but this checkpoint's own migration (`supabase/migrations/20260801150000_create_customer_portal_customer_profile.sql`) deliberately does not make either customer-writable. `parent_account_id`/`merged_into_id`/`org_unit_id`/`owner_user_id` are excluded for the unrelated, structural reason that they carry zero customer-facing meaning (tenant org structure, staff CRM ownership, account hierarchy/merge lineage) — not disclosed as a gap, since no plausible reading of the source prompt asks for those to be customer-editable. `legal_name`/`tax_id` ARE included in `app.get_customer_portal_account_profile`'s own READ projection (design decision 3 of the migration) — a customer can always see their own registered legal identity, rendered locked in the UI with an explanatory note, never hidden.

**Item 2 — `app.list_customer_portal_account_contacts` is read-only; no contact change-request table was built.** `app.contact_links` (COM-145/COM-155) is Commercial-owned CRM data with its own existing staff-only mutation surface (`app.link_contact_to_record`, gated on `COM:Edit` + `app.can_access_record`). A customer-initiated contact add/edit/remove-with-approval workflow mirroring this same checkpoint's own account-profile change-request shape was considered and rejected for this checkpoint specifically: it would require its own table, its own field-shape validation, its own staff-decision RPC — a second capability-sized addition alongside the account-profile one, exceeding this prompt's own explicit file/migration budget (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations; this checkpoint already uses 1 migration for the account-profile path).

**Live effect:** a customer viewing `/customer-profile` today can propose a change to their own account's trade name or billing address (staff-reviewed before it takes effect) and can see their own account's legal name/tax id/customer status and linked contacts, but cannot request a legal-name/tax-id correction or a contact change through the portal — they must contact their account administrator/CargoGrid support out of band for either, exactly as the locked-field note in the UI states. Not a security issue: no data is fabricated, no existing caller is affected, and every writable field this prompt's own business rules actually require (trade name, billing address) is fully built with a real staff-reviewed (`COM:Approve`) approval workflow applying to the canonical `app.accounts` row in the same transaction as the decision.

**Not fixed here** — both are deliberate, disclosed charter-boundary decisions, not oversights: item 1 because a legal-identity change genuinely has compliance/KYC implications this prompt's own "customer profile maintenance" charter does not cover (mirrors the source prompt's own "tax/legal... require configured authorization/approval" business rule, read as "not yet configured, therefore not yet self-service" rather than silently building an under-governed shortcut); item 2 because building it would double this checkpoint's own already-bounded scope for a screen the source prompt's own requirement ("account/site/contact/address preferences") is already honestly satisfied by via a read-only projection (ADR-0024 Part A governs reads; nothing requires every new read to also grow a write path). **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for both (no data fabricated, no existing caller affected, the locked/read-only fields are always shown truthfully, never hidden or silently editable). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks these up: item 1 — a dedicated legal-identity-change capability with a real KYC/compliance review step (likely MFA/RPD-023-gated per the source prompt's own privileged-action business rule), separate from this checkpoint's own trade-name/billing-address workflow; item 2 — a `app.customer_portal_contact_change_requests` table mirroring this checkpoint's own `app.customer_portal_profile_change_requests` shape, with its own staff-decision RPC applying to `app.contact_links`/`app.contacts` in the same transaction.

### ISS-2026-124 — `app.get_customer_portal_invoice`/`app.list_customer_portal_invoices` omit `customer_account_id` from their own projection, unlike every sibling capability's equivalent RPC (Phase 8, Batch 3 Tier C review, correctness/concurrency lens, OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-17` at Batch 3's own Tier C review close (`CG-S13-CPL-012..016`, Prompts 310-314), correctness/concurrency lens.

**Code:** `app.get_customer_portal_invoice`/`app.list_customer_portal_invoices` (`supabase/migrations/20260801120000_create_customer_portal_invoice_billing_visibility.sql`, CPL-311) both `RETURNS TABLE (id, invoice_number, currency, status, subtotal_amount, tax_amount, total_amount, issue_date, due_date, record_version, updated_at)` — no `customer_account_id`/`account_id` column of any kind. Every sibling capability's own equivalent RPC includes the owning-account id in its own projection: CPL-309's `app.get_customer_portal_inventory_balance`/`app.list_customer_portal_inventory_balances` and CPL-310's `app.get_customer_portal_outbound_order`/`app.list_customer_portal_outbound_orders` both include `owner_account_id`; CPL-312's `app.list_customer_portal_receipts` (this same batch, landed one migration after CPL-311) includes `customer_account_id` directly. CPL-311 is the one outlier.

**Live effect:** a `customer_user` whose Layer 4 membership resolves to more than one account (a real, supported shape since CPL-300's own widened `app.resolve_customer_account_scope` and `app.customer_portal_account_memberships` multi-account grant table) sees all of their own invoices correctly (never another account's, never a leaked one — the scope gate itself is unaffected by this finding) but has no field in `app.list_customer_portal_invoices`'s own result to tell WHICH of their own accounts a given invoice row belongs to — a completeness/UX gap, not a security or data-correctness one. A single-account customer (today's common case for most Phase 8 fixtures) never notices, since every row is trivially "their one account" either way.

**Not fixed at this Tier C review pass** — adding the column to both `RETURNS TABLE` shapes is itself a safe `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` (both are new-this-batch functions, no already-applied-migration constraint), but a complete, verifiable fix also requires updating `server/contracts/customer-portal-invoice/customer-portal-invoice.ts` (the Zod row schema and its `parseCustomerPortalInvoice`-shaped parser), `server/queries/customer-portal-invoice.ts` (the raw-row mapping), and at least one of the two customer-invoice UI routes (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/customer-invoices/`) to actually surface the new field — otherwise the fix is present in the database but invisible and unverified at the layer a reviewer or a customer would actually see. This four-file, cross-layer shape did not meet this bounded Tier C fix pass's own "fix Low findings only if trivial, otherwise disclose" bar (`docs/standards/BUILD_EXECUTION_PROTOCOL.md` governing instruction for this exact pass), and is not a Critical/High/Medium defect this pass is unconditionally required to fix regardless of size. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (no data fabricated or leaked; every field this RPC currently returns remains correct and customer-safe; only a multi-account customer loses a "which account" cue from this one RPC). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: add `customer_account_id uuid` to both `RETURNS TABLE` shapes (`v_invoice.customer_account_id`/`i.customer_account_id` respectively — the column already exists on `app.finance_invoices`, already used internally by the gate, just never projected outward), add the matching Zod field + parser update, and surface it in the invoice list/detail UI (e.g. the account's own trade name, resolved client-side from the account-switcher context CPL-300's own UI already carries) — mirroring CPL-310's own `owner_account_id` precedent exactly.

### ISS-2026-125 — Customer User Management (CPL-315): no MFA/step-up primitive and no session/token-revocation primitive exist repository-wide (standing disclosures), plus a real, unfixed "last active account_admin" gap remains open in CPL-300's own already-`VERIFIED` `set_customer_portal_account_membership_status` (Phase 8, Batch 4, `CG-S13-CPL-017`, Medium for item 3 / Low for items 1-2, OPEN)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-017` (Prompt 315, Customer User Management), the first prompt of Batch 4 — an additive extension of CPL-300's own already-`VERIFIED` invite/accept/status-management machinery (`supabase/migrations/20260801010000_create_customer_portal_account_scope.sql`).

**Item 1 — no MFA/current-authorization (RPD-023) mechanism exists anywhere in this repository.** Confirmed again this checkpoint (grep-verified repository-wide, not merely assumed) — identical to CPL-300 §9's own disclosure ("No MFA/step-up-auth mechanism exists anywhere in this repository yet") and CPL-314's own residual-limitations section. This prompt's own source spec (§16, §24) names MFA/current-authorization for "privileged customer-admin, reward approval, export and support actions" as a required control for high-risk role/scope changes. `app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/customer-portal-users/actions.ts`'s own role-change/suspend/revoke Server Actions carry a client-side `confirm()` prompt (mirroring `app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/hris/employees/[masterRecordId]/employee-detail-panel.tsx`'s own established `confirmReason` pattern) as a UX safeguard against an accidental click — this is explicitly NOT represented as satisfying RPD-023 anywhere in this checkpoint's own code comments or this entry. The real, and only, authorization boundary is the server-side `app.actor_is_active_customer_portal_account_admin` check every RPC in this whole capability performs on every call, live, never cached.

**Item 2 — no session/token/JWT-revocation primitive exists anywhere in this repository** (grep-verified this checkpoint: zero hits for `revoke_session`/`invalidate_session`/`revoke_token`/`invalidate_token` anywhere in `supabase/migrations/`, `server/`, `app/`, `lib/`). The source prompt's own §24 business rule ("Revocation invalidates sessions, tokens, signed URLs, exports and saved views where applicable") is therefore not literally implementable by this or any prior Phase 8 checkpoint — building a new, standalone session-invalidation mechanism as a side effect of this one capability prompt would be a new, out-of-scope, unreviewed primitive, not a bounded fix. The real, already-shipped mitigation, disclosed honestly rather than papered over: `app.set_customer_portal_account_membership_status`'s own comment (CPL-300) already states this exact tradeoff, and every read RPC across this whole capability — including this checkpoint's own two new ones, `app.list_customer_portal_account_membership_access_reviews`/`app.list_customer_portal_account_memberships_for_access_review` — re-checks the caller's own current, live status/role/authority on every single call, never from a cached session claim. A revoked or role-demoted member therefore loses (or gains) access on their very next call, not merely "eventually" — the closest structural equivalent to session invalidation this repository's own architecture provides.

**Item 3 — a real, live, unfixed authority gap, discovered while designing this checkpoint's own last-account_admin guard (design decision 3 of `supabase/migrations/20260801170000_create_customer_portal_user_management.sql`).** `app.update_customer_portal_account_membership_role` (this checkpoint's own new RPC) rejects a role change that would leave an account with zero active `account_admin` rows. Reasoning through why this guard was necessary at all surfaced that the IDENTICAL gap already exists, unfixed, in `app.set_customer_portal_account_membership_status` — CPL-300's own already-`VERIFIED`, already-applied function that this prompt may not edit in place. Nothing in that function stops the sole active `account_admin` on an account from suspending or revoking themselves (or the account's only other `account_admin`), and once that happens the account has NO self-service recovery path: `app.grant_initial_customer_portal_account_admin` (the one staff-facing bootstrap escape hatch) is a no-op once any row already exists for that identity+account — it returns the existing (now suspended/revoked) row unchanged, it does not re-promote or reactivate it. A tenant would need direct database intervention (or a brand-new capability that does not exist today) to recover self-service account administration for that account.

**Live effect:** this is a real, exploitable-by-a-legitimate-actor-against-themselves footgun (not a cross-tenant/cross-account security leak — the actor can only ever affect their own account's own admin set), not yet observed as a live incident, disclosed proactively rather than silently left for a future reviewer or a real customer to discover the hard way.

**Not fixed here** — item 3's fix is a genuine, additive `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` migration against `app.set_customer_portal_account_membership_status` specifically (mirroring this checkpoint's own `update_customer_portal_account_membership_role` guard shape: lock the full active-admin set for the account before deciding, reject a suspend/revoke that would leave zero), never an edit to the already-applied `20260801010000_create_customer_portal_account_scope.sql` file — out of this prompt's own bounded scope, which owns only its own new RPCs, not CPL-300's. Items 1-2 are standing, repository-wide infrastructure gaps (MFA/step-up authorization; session/token revocation) no single capability prompt is chartered to close on its own, per CPL-300 §9's/CPL-314's own identical prior disclosure and this task's own explicit instruction not to fabricate either primitive. **Status `OPEN`.** Severity split: Medium for item 3 (a real, live, self-inflictable authority gap in already-shipped code, narrow blast radius, no cross-tenant/cross-account exposure); Low for items 1-2 (unchanged, already-accepted repository-wide residual risk this prompt does not worsen). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks these up: item 3 — the additive hardening migration described above, plus a live db-test regression proof (a 2-admin account, one self-demotes to leave the true last, the last is rejected) mirroring this checkpoint's own `customer-user-management.sql` coverage; items 1-2 — a dedicated, repository-wide MFA/step-up-authorization capability and a dedicated, repository-wide session/token-revocation capability, neither of which exists on any current Phase 8 execution-index row.

**Correction (2026-08-20, CPL-326, `CG-S13-CPL-028`) — item 1's own citation corrected, not deleted, per this file's own "do not delete resolved issues; mark RESOLVED/SUPERSEDED" maintenance rule applied here to a citation fix rather than a status change.** Item 1 above states the MFA/RPD-023 gap is "already disclosed identically at CPL-300 §9 and CPL-314." `ISS-2026-138` (registered at `CPL-325`, `CG-S13-CPL-027`) independently grep-confirmed `docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-314.md` contains **zero** mentions of MFA/RPD-023/step-up in any form — that citation is false, and was re-confirmed false again directly by this checkpoint (`grep -ic "RPD-023\|MFA\|step-up" docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-314.md` → `0`). The correct standing disclosure lineage for the repository-wide RPD-023 gap is CPL-300 §9 only, plus every Phase 8 build log CPL-301 through CPL-313 and CPL-315 (each independently confirmed to carry 1-4 mentions per `ISS-2026-138`'s own grep) — never CPL-314, and, per `ISS-2026-138` itself, never CPL-316 through CPL-323 either (the entire back half of Phase 8, including reward approval and fraud release, silently carries no RPD-023 disclosure of its own at all). See `ISS-2026-138` below for the full finding; this note only corrects item 1's own false forward-reference, it does not re-litigate the underlying gap.

### ISS-2026-126 — Loyalty earning evaluation is on-demand/staff-triggered only; no automatic job or Finance-side trigger wires `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice` to a real payment event yet (Phase 8, Batch 4, CPL-316, `CG-S13-CPL-018`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-018` (Prompt 316, Loyalty Program and Earning) — the FIRST-EVER Loyalty domain capability in this repository (ADR-0024 Part D), a deliberate scope decision made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801180000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_program_earning.sql`, not a defect found afterward.

**The gap.** Prompt 316's own §21 main flow reads: "Finance marks an eligible invoice paid; loyalty engine evaluates active program version and writes an idempotent earning ledger entry." This checkpoint builds `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice` as a real, complete, idempotent, fully-working RPC (verified live: idempotent on `(tenant_id, 'ar-open-item:' || ar_open_item_id)`, rejects unpaid/held/inactive-program/unpublished-rule/below-minimum invoices, computes the reward per the currently published rule version) — but nothing calls it automatically the moment `app.finance_ar_open_items.status` actually flips to `'paid'`. Today it is invoked on demand only, via a staff/tenant-admin action in this checkpoint's own new admin UI (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/admin/loyalty`, "Evaluate earning for a paid invoice").

**Why no automatic wiring was built.** `app.apply_finance_ar_allocation` (FIN-198, `20260729100000_create_finance_accounts_receivable.sql`) is the ONE function that ever sets `status = 'paid'` on an AR open item, and it is an already-APPLIED migration this task may not edit in place — confirmed by direct read before writing this migration, not assumed. The only additive alternative — a new `AFTER UPDATE` trigger this migration attaches directly onto Finance-owned `app.finance_ar_open_items` — was considered and rejected: it would make Loyalty logic fire silently inside a Finance-owned write path with no Finance-side review point, exactly the kind of unreviewed cross-domain coupling ADR-0024 Part D's own handoff discipline (`prepare_finance_*_from_*`, "read another domain's already-committed state, never write into it") is designed to avoid. Registering a new `job_type` value with the existing PLT-132 background-job engine (`app.jobs`, `20260719180000_create_background_job_framework.sql`) was also considered — additive in principle (a `DROP`+`ADD CONSTRAINT` widening of `jobs_job_type_check`, the same non-destructive technique PLT-131 itself already used) — but a complete, honest implementation would also require a real job handler/worker wiring, a call site enqueuing the job at the actual moment of payment, and its own db-test regression proof, which together are a genuinely new, capability-sized addition beyond this prompt's own bounded scope (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations; this checkpoint already uses close to that budget for program/rule-version/account/earning-event CRUD plus both UIs).

**Live effect:** a paid invoice does NOT automatically earn loyalty points/cashback the instant Finance marks it paid — a staff member (or a future scheduled job) must call `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice` for that specific AR open item. No data is fabricated and no existing caller is affected; the evaluation logic itself is complete, correct, and idempotent (a genuine "trigger mechanism is deferred, not the evaluation logic" gap, per this prompt's own explicit escape-valve instruction: "if not, disclose plainly ... that earning evaluation is currently on-demand/manually-triggered only ... rather than fully automatic").

**Not fixed here** — both realistic additive fixes (a Finance-table trigger; a new PLT-132 job type plus worker plus enqueue call site) are each a genuinely new, reviewable, capability-sized decision outside this prompt's own bounded scope, and the source prompt's own §"Callable trigger mechanism" text explicitly authorizes disclosing this as a real, honest scope boundary rather than building either shortcut. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (no data fabricated or leaked; the real, complete, idempotent RPC exists and is reachable today via the admin UI; no existing caller or test is affected; the business impact is operational latency — earning is delayed until a staff action or a future job runs, never wrong once it does run). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: either (a) a dedicated additive migration registering a new `loyalty_earning_evaluation` `job_type` on `app.jobs` (widening `jobs_job_type_check` non-destructively) plus a worker that calls `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice` and a real enqueue call site, or (b) a reviewed, disclosed `AFTER UPDATE OF status` trigger on `app.finance_ar_open_items` (Finance-side sign-off required, since it touches a Finance-owned table), each with its own live db-test regression proof (a payment-allocation event that reaches `status='paid'` results in exactly one new `app.loyalty_earning_events` row, automatically, without a manual RPC call).

### ISS-2026-127 — Membership Tier (CPL-317): recalculation is on-demand/staff-triggered only, a program without a base tier raises a real error rather than defaulting, and `tier_definition_version_id` is structurally identical to `to_tier_id` in this checkpoint's own flattened design (Phase 8, Batch 4, `CG-S13-CPL-019`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-019` (Prompt 317, Membership Tier) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801190000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_membership_tier.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — on-demand recalculation only.** `app.recalculate_customer_loyalty_tier` is a real, complete, idempotent, fully-working RPC — but nothing calls it automatically on a schedule (e.g. nightly, or the moment a new `app.loyalty_earning_events` row posts). Today it is invoked on demand only, via a staff/tenant-admin action in this checkpoint's own new admin UI (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/admin/loyalty-tiers`, "Recalculate tier"). This mirrors CPL-316's own already-accepted `ISS-2026-126` precedent for the sibling earning-evaluation gap exactly — registering a scheduled-job wiring (a new `job_type` on `app.jobs` plus a worker plus a real enqueue call site, or a call from `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice`'s own success path) is a genuinely new, capability-sized addition beyond this prompt's own bounded scope (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations), not attempted here.

**Item 2 — no auto-created base tier.** This checkpoint's own business-rule reading (migration design decision 8) expects a program's own published tier-definition set to include a `threshold_value = 0` base tier, so every enrolled account resolves to SOME tier on its first recalculation. This migration does not auto-create such a tier for any program — that is tenant/program configuration's own job. A program published without a base rung causes `app.recalculate_customer_loyalty_tier` to raise a real, loud `no_eligible_tier_definition` error (live-verified in this checkpoint's own db-test, the "Gapped Program" fixture) rather than silently defaulting an account to an arbitrary tier or leaving it in an undefined state.

**Item 3 — `tier_definition_version_id` structurally identical to `to_tier_id`.** The source prompt's own literal column list for `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` names both `to_tier_id` and `tier_definition_version_id` as separate columns. This checkpoint's own tier-definition schema collapses "tier identity" and "tier version" onto one row per version (mirroring CPL-316's own `loyalty_program_rule_versions` collapse), so the two columns always carry the identical value in this checkpoint — enforced by a real table `CHECK` constraint (`latm_version_id_matches_to_tier_check`), never merely a convention. Both are kept as distinct, independently-named columns (never collapsed into one) so a future capability that ever splits "tier identity" from "tier version" (the way `app.loyalty_programs`/`app.loyalty_program_rule_versions` already split at the program level) can widen `tier_definition_version_id`'s own meaning additively, without a breaking rename of `to_tier_id`.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 mirrors an already-accepted repository-wide-shaped precedent (`ISS-2026-126`); item 2 is a disclosed design boundary that fails loudly, never silently; item 3 is a deliberate, disclosed design choice recorded in the migration's own header, not an oversight. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, a dedicated additive migration registering a new job type plus worker plus enqueue call site (mirroring `ISS-2026-126`'s own recommended fix shape); item 2, none required — tenant/program configuration discipline, optionally a future onboarding-time linter that warns a published program lacks a `threshold_value = 0` tier; item 3, none required unless a future capability genuinely needs independent tier-identity/tier-version tracking.

### ISS-2026-128 — Points Ledger (CPL-318): earning-event-to-lot conversion and lot expiry are on-demand/staff-triggered only; lot expiry window is a caller-supplied parameter rather than a persisted per-program config; the FIFO consumption primitive has no customer-facing redemption trigger yet (Phase 8, Batch 4, `CG-S13-CPL-020`, OPEN — items 1-2 only, item 3 `RESOLVED` 2026-08-20 at CPL-324, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-020` (Prompt 318, Points Ledger) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801200000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_points_ledger.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — earning-event-to-lot conversion and lot expiry are on-demand/staff-triggered only.** `app.post_loyalty_points_earned` (converts a CPL-316 points-type earning event into a real point lot + earn ledger entry) and `app.expire_loyalty_point_lots` (scans and expires due lots tenant-wide) are both real, complete, idempotent, fully-working RPCs — but nothing calls either automatically. Today both are invoked on demand only, via staff actions in this checkpoint's own new admin UI (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/admin/loyalty-points`, "Sync points from earning event" / "Run expiry scan"). This mirrors CPL-316's own already-accepted `ISS-2026-126` and CPL-317's own `ISS-2026-127` item 1 precedent exactly — registering a scheduled-job wiring (a new `job_type` on `app.jobs` plus a worker plus a real enqueue call site) is a genuinely new, capability-sized addition beyond this prompt's own bounded scope (normally 5-15 files, at most 1-3 additive migrations), not attempted here.

**Item 2 — lot expiry window is a caller-supplied, bounded parameter (`p_expiry_days`, 1-3650, default 365), not a persisted per-(tenant,program) config.** A real, working, bounded policy — not a magic hardcoded constant, not an unbounded free-form input — but a lighter-weight, disclosed scope decision than CPL-317's own persisted `review_period_days` column precedent. Since the same staff action always defaults to the same 365-day value in this checkpoint's own admin UI, live behavior is consistent in practice, but nothing in the database enforces that two different staff members convert two different earning events for the SAME program with the SAME expiry window if they type different values into the form. Migration design decision 4 discloses this explicitly.

**Item 3 — `app.consume_loyalty_points_fifo` is a real, complete, live-proven (FIFO-by-expiry ordering, whole-redemption idempotency, negative-balance prevention under both a single-session over-consumption attempt and a real two-process concurrent-race attempt) ledger-side primitive, but no customer-facing redemption UI or reward/voucher catalog exists yet to call it from.** No reward catalog capability exists anywhere in this repository yet (CPL-316's own disclosed precedent: "discount/voucher issuance is CPL-319's own scope"). `server/mutations/customer-portal-loyalty-points.ts` wraps the primitive for future use; nothing in this checkpoint's own UI calls it. Mirrors `ISS-2026-126`/`ISS-2026-127`'s own "real primitive exists; nothing calls it automatically/from an end-user surface yet" disclosure shape exactly. **`RESOLVED` (2026-08-20, CPL-324 Integrated Verification, `CG-S13-CPL-026`) — a real production caller now exists.** Independently re-derived, not accepted from a prior lens report on its word: `app.submit_loyalty_redemption` (`supabase/migrations/20260801230000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_redemption_approval_fulfillment.sql:770`, `grant execute ... to authenticated, service_role` at line 1529) composes `app._compose_loyalty_redemption_decision` (line 596), which calls `app.reserve_loyalty_reward_stock_unit` and `app.consume_loyalty_points_fifo` at the actual moment of redemption (CPL-320's own reward catalogue supplies the reward/voucher catalog this item's own text said did not exist). This item's own text is stale as of CPL-321 (Batch 5, 2026-08-18) and is corrected here rather than left to mislead a future reader; items 1 and 2 remain independently re-confirmed accurate and `OPEN`.

**Not fixed here** — items 1 and 2 mirror already-accepted, repository-wide-shaped precedent from this same Loyalty domain's own two prior checkpoints (`ISS-2026-126`, `ISS-2026-127`); neither is a silent gap. Item 3 is `RESOLVED` (see above). **Status `OPEN`** (items 1-2), Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including live-proven negative-balance prevention under a genuine concurrent race; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, a dedicated additive migration registering new job types plus workers plus enqueue call sites (mirroring `ISS-2026-126`'s own recommended fix shape), ideally chained directly off `app.evaluate_customer_loyalty_earning_for_paid_invoice`'s own success path for item 1's earning half; item 2, an additive `app.loyalty_point_program_configs` table (tenant_id, program_id, points_expiry_days) this checkpoint's own migration deliberately did not build, mirroring CPL-317's own `review_period_days` precedent; item 3, whichever future capability builds a reward/voucher catalog (CPL-319+) should call `app.consume_loyalty_points_fifo` directly rather than reinventing FIFO consumption.

### ISS-2026-129 — Cashback Discount Voucher (CPL-319): no Finance liability-handoff/reconciliation mechanism yet (explicitly CPL-323's own future scope); issuance/expiry are on-demand/staff-triggered only; entitlement value is a currency amount only, no percentage-based voucher model (Phase 8, Batch 4, `CG-S13-CPL-021`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-021` (Prompt 319, Cashback Discount Voucher, the fifth and final prompt of Batch 4) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801210000_create_customer_portal_cashback_discount_voucher.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — no Finance liability-handoff/reconciliation mechanism.** ADR-0024 Part D's own general shape for Loyalty-liability-to-Finance names a Loyalty-owned handoff-batch table plus an idempotent generator function plus a Finance-side acknowledgement RPC (mirroring HRT-282's `prepare_finance_*_from_*` shape), and a FIN-209-shaped execute/resolve-then-certify reconciliation pair. None of that is built in this checkpoint — this checkpoint's own orchestrating task instruction explicitly named it `CPL-323`'s own future scope ("Liability Reconciliation Analytics") and directed this checkpoint to record entitlement value/currency/status/issued_at/source cleanly and accurately instead, so a future `CPL-323` can build the handoff/reconciliation layer on top. `app.loyalty_benefit_entitlements`/`app.loyalty_benefit_entitlement_events` together are real, complete, accurate source-of-truth records (never placeholder/fake) — only the Finance-facing handoff/reconciliation layer itself is deferred.

**Item 2 — issuance/expiry are on-demand/staff-triggered only.** `app.issue_loyalty_benefit_entitlement` and `app.expire_loyalty_benefit_entitlements` are both real, complete, idempotent, fully-working RPCs — but nothing calls either automatically (no scheduled job, no automatic trigger off a Commercial/Finance/Operations event). Today both are invoked on demand only, via staff actions in this checkpoint's own new admin UI (`app/(tenant)/[tenantSlug]/admin/loyalty-benefits`, "Issue benefit" / "Run expiry scan"). This mirrors CPL-316/317/318's own already-accepted `ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128` precedent exactly — registering a scheduled-job wiring or an automatic issuance trigger off a real business event (e.g. a paid invoice, a completed shipment) is a genuinely new, capability-sized addition beyond this prompt's own bounded scope, not attempted here.

**Item 3 — entitlement value is a currency amount only, no percentage-based voucher model.** This checkpoint's own schema requires a real `currency` on every entitlement (cashback, discount, and voucher alike) and treats `value_amount`/`value_cap` uniformly as currency-denominated amounts (e.g. "$15 off"), not a percentage (e.g. "20% off"). The source prompt's own literal schema never distinguishes a percentage model, and a currency-amount model covers every literal business rule this checkpoint had to satisfy; a future checkpoint that needs percentage-based vouchers would add a new, disclosed `value_kind` dimension rather than overloading `value_amount`'s own current meaning.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 is an explicit, orchestrator-directed scope boundary (not a gap this checkpoint could have closed within its own bounded file budget); item 2 mirrors an already-accepted repository-wide-shaped precedent (`ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`); item 3 is a deliberate, disclosed design simplification, not an oversight. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including live-proven value_cap enforcement, anti-enumerating redemption, and fraud-hold blocking under adversarial testing; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, `CPL-323` itself, per its own already-scoped "Liability Reconciliation Analytics" task; item 2, a dedicated additive migration registering new job types plus workers plus enqueue call sites (mirroring `ISS-2026-126`'s own recommended fix shape); item 3, none required unless a future capability genuinely needs a percentage-based voucher.

### ISS-2026-130 — no Supreme-Admin-exception override mechanism (RPD-022) exists yet for any of the four Loyalty ledger tables (Phase 8, Batch 4 Tier C review, `CG-S13-CPL-018/019/020/021`, `RESOLVED` 2026-08-20 at CPL-325, was Medium)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at the Batch 4 (`CPL-315..319`) Tier C review, cross-prompt-integration lens: `docs/architecture/06_RLS_RBAC_WORKSTREAM.md` §4 names `point_ledger`/`cashback_ledger` inside the repository's `append_only_ledger` policy family, §8 (RPD-022) requires a distinct Supreme-Admin-exception RLS policy granting `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on every such table (the disclosed, never-tamper-proof audit trail is the accountability mechanism substituting for true immutability), and §13 calls that per-table policy a Phase-8 release-blocker gate. None of `app.loyalty_earning_events` (CPL-316), `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` (CPL-317), `app.loyalty_point_ledger_entries` (CPL-318), or `app.loyalty_benefit_entitlement_events` (CPL-319) implements it — each grants, at most, `select`/`insert` to `service_role` only, with zero `UPDATE`/`DELETE` grant to any role, staff or Supreme Admin alike.

CPL-318's own migration (design decision 13) did cite RPD-022 and disclose the gap, but its original citation text conflated §8's "residual risk... RISK-004, never closed" language (which describes the audit trail's own alterability, a property of the mechanism once it exists) with a justification for not building the override mechanism at all (which §13 separately, explicitly calls a release blocker) — corrected at this same Tier C review pass. CPL-316/317/319 carried no RPD-022 citation of any kind before this review; CPL-319 in particular built the closest concrete realization of "cashback_ledger" (`app.loyalty_benefit_entitlement_events`) with zero mention of Supreme Admin or RPD-022 anywhere in its own file.

Mitigating context, confirmed directly: this is not a novel gap this batch invented. `app.inventory_movements` (`supabase/migrations/20260730190000_create_advanced_tms_inventory_ledger.sql`, this batch's own required-read precedent file and an already-`VERIFIED` append-only ledger table) has the identical gap — grep-confirmed zero mention of `is_supreme_admin`/`supreme_admin`/`FIN-204`/`RPD-022` anywhere in that migration. The absence makes these ledgers MORE immutable, not less secure — no live vulnerability results; the only thing missing is the disclosed EXCEPTION mechanism a Supreme Admin would use for a genuine, audited correction.

Live-verified this checkpoint (`scripts/db-tests/customer-portal-loyalty-ledger-supreme-admin-override.sql`, and re-verified against the full `db:test` suite): a raw `UPDATE`/`DELETE` with no actor context is blocked; an ordinary tenant staff actor holding `LYL:Configure` but NOT a `supreme_admin` principal membership is ALSO blocked (RPD-022 is Supreme-Admin-only, never any elevated tenant role); a genuine Supreme Admin's mutation succeeds and is captured to `app.audit_logs` with correct before/after values and actor identity, on two of the five tables directly (the shared trigger function is identical code across all five, so this is not five independent proofs, but two full round-trip proofs plus grant/architecture confirmation on the remaining three).

**Deliberately does NOT retroactively cover `app.inventory_movements`** (a pre-existing, already-`VERIFIED` Phase 5 ledger with the identical gap) **or any other pre-Phase-8 `append_only_ledger`-family table** — this checkpoint's own charter has the authority to decide for Phase 8's own tables specifically, not repository-wide; a dedicated, future cross-cutting task remains the correct vehicle for `app.inventory_movements` and any other phase's own ledgers, exactly as this issue's own original disclosure named it.

**New residual disclosure — `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` carries the identical gap and was NOT included in this migration.** This table was named in this issue's own ORIGINAL four-table list (Batch 4, before `CPL-320`/`CPL-321` existed) but was omitted from this checkpoint's own explicit 5-table remediation scope (which instead named the two newer Batch-5 tables, `app.loyalty_reward_stock_reservations`/`app.loyalty_redemption_events`, that postdate this issue's own original disclosure). Grep-confirmed: `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` still grants only `select, insert` to `service_role` (`supabase/migrations/20260801190000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_membership_tier.sql:1192`), zero `UPDATE`/`DELETE` to any role.
