### ISS-2026-131 — Reward Catalogue (CPL-320): the actual redemption/consume-stock transaction does not exist yet (explicitly CPL-321's own future scope); the real, race-safe stock-reservation primitive has no production caller yet; reward media/config UI has no file-upload flow of its own (Phase 8, Batch 5, `CG-S13-CPL-022`, OPEN — item 3 only, items 1-2 `RESOLVED` 2026-08-20 at CPL-324, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-17` at `CG-S13-CPL-022` (Prompt 320, Reward Catalogue, the first prompt of Batch 5) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801220000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_reward_catalogue.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — no redemption/consume-stock transaction.** This checkpoint's own scope boundary (its own orchestrating task instruction, and the source prompt's own downstream note naming `CPL-321`, "Redemption Approval and Fulfillment," as the next capability) is the CATALOGUE only: reward definitions, eligibility criteria, stock/availability configuration, effective-dated scheduling, terms, and customer-safe presentation. No RPC anywhere in this migration decrements stock, creates a redemption record, or debits a customer's own points/tier standing against a reward. `app.list_customer_portal_loyalty_rewards`/`app.get_customer_portal_loyalty_reward` compute a live, honest `eligible`/`locked`/`out_of_stock`/`unavailable` projection, but nothing in this checkpoint lets a customer actually act on an `eligible` reward. This is the identical, already-accepted "build the read-safe projection, defer the actual transaction" scope shape CPL-318's own `app.consume_loyalty_points_fifo` (no reward catalog existed yet to call it from) and CPL-319's own Finance-handoff boundary (`ISS-2026-129` item 1) already established — here the shapes reverse (the catalogue exists, the redemption consumer does not). **`RESOLVED` (2026-08-20, CPL-324 Integrated Verification, `CG-S13-CPL-026`) — `CPL-321`'s own migration built exactly this transaction.** Independently re-derived, not accepted from a prior lens report on its word: `app.submit_loyalty_redemption`/`app.decide_loyalty_redemption` (`supabase/migrations/20260801230000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_redemption_approval_fulfillment.sql`, `grant execute ... to authenticated, service_role` at lines 1529-1530) create a real `app.loyalty_redemptions` row and, on approval, atomically decrement stock and debit points via `app._compose_loyalty_redemption_decision`.

**Item 2 — `app.reserve_loyalty_reward_stock_unit` (the real, race-safe stock-reservation primitive, migration design decision 7) has no production caller yet.** It is a real, complete, live-proven-under-a-genuine-two-process-concurrent-race primitive (this checkpoint's own db-test, `scripts/db-tests/customer-loyalty-reward-catalogue.sql`, reuses `scripts/db-tests/wms-picking-concurrency-helper.sh` exactly as CPL-318's own negative-balance race proof did) — but nothing in this checkpoint's own admin/customer UI calls it (there is no real reservation event to trigger yet, since redemption itself does not exist). `server/mutations/customer-portal-loyalty-rewards.ts` wraps it for completeness/future use, mirroring `ISS-2026-128` item 3's own identical "the primitive exists, nothing calls it in production yet" disclosure shape exactly. `CPL-321` is expected to call this primitive (or compose an equivalent it builds itself) at the actual moment of redemption, after independently re-validating the customer's own eligibility and the reward's own effective-date window — this primitive deliberately does not re-check either on its own. **`RESOLVED` (2026-08-20, CPL-324 Integrated Verification, `CG-S13-CPL-026`) — a real production caller now exists.** Confirmed by direct code read: `app._compose_loyalty_redemption_decision` (`20260801230000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_redemption_approval_fulfillment.sql:638`) calls `app.reserve_loyalty_reward_stock_unit` inside the same composed transaction `app.submit_loyalty_redemption`/`app.decide_loyalty_redemption` drive.

**Item 3 — no new file-upload UI.** Reward media/terms documents reuse `app.files` via a foreign key (`file_id`), per this checkpoint's own explicit instruction to never invent a second file/upload table. The admin reward-create/edit form accepts an existing `app.files.id` by direct text entry (a staff member pastes an id already produced by another upload surface, e.g. the Document Center) rather than offering its own drag-and-drop uploader. A real, complete, working file reference — malware-scan-gated visibility, `app.file_access_logs` audit trail, no fabricated signed URL — is fully built and tested; only a dedicated uploader widget is deferred, a disclosed scope simplification consistent with this checkpoint's own "5-15 files, 1-3 additive migrations" sizing discipline. Independently re-confirmed still accurate this same checkpoint (CPL-324) — no dedicated uploader widget exists anywhere in the admin reward form as of this pass.

**Not fixed here** — item 3 is a deliberate, disclosed design simplification, not an oversight, and remains `OPEN`. Items 1 and 2 are `RESOLVED` (see above — `CPL-321` closed both on its own already-scoped terms). **Status `OPEN`** (item 3 only), Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including live-proven optimistic-concurrency NULL-bypass regressions across all five version-checked functions, a real two-process concurrent stock-reservation race, and a structurally-provable internal-cost/vendor-ref-never-leaked guarantee; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, `CPL-321` itself, per its own already-scoped "Redemption Approval and Fulfillment" task, composing `app.reserve_loyalty_reward_stock_unit` (or an equivalent) after its own eligibility/effective-date re-validation; item 2, none required beyond `CPL-321` wiring a real caller; item 3, a future capability could add a proper file-picker/uploader to the admin reward form, reusing PLT-128's own `app.initiate_file_upload` the same way the Document Center's own UI already does.

### ISS-2026-132 — Redemption Approval and Fulfillment (CPL-321): a genuine, unassisted customer_user self-service redemption never auto-approves synchronously, regardless of reward_type; discount_voucher entitlement value is sourced from the reward's own staff-only internal_cost; no notification/retry/DLQ mechanism exists yet (Phase 8, Batch 5, `CG-S13-CPL-023`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-18` at `CG-S13-CPL-023` (Prompt 321, Redemption Approval and Fulfillment, the second prompt of Batch 5) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801230000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_redemption_approval_fulfillment.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — this checkpoint's own most consequential architectural resolution: composing `app.reserve_loyalty_reward_stock_unit`/`app.consume_loyalty_points_fifo` (both real, already-shipped, staff/system-only, `LYL:Edit`-gated primitives — CPL-320/318's own literal authority label) from a genuinely unassisted `customer_user` session is structurally impossible without either widening either primitive's own RBAC gate (forbidden — ADR-0024 Part B, `ISS-2026-040`) or provisioning a wholly new, tenant-scoped automated "system" identity (a genuinely new, cross-cutting, per-tenant-provisioning capability, well beyond this single prompt's own bounded 5-15-file scope).** Confirmed directly, not assumed: `app.role_assignments` has exactly one `insert` call site in this entire repository (`app.assign_role_to_user`, a staff-only administrative RPC), which the customer-portal invite flow never touches — a genuine `customer_user` identity therefore never holds `LYL:Edit` in this repository's own established provisioning discipline. This checkpoint's resolution: `app.submit_loyalty_redemption` (dual authority, mirroring CPL-319's own `app.redeem_loyalty_benefit_entitlement` design decision 5) always creates the real portal-owned intent record (`app.loyalty_redemptions`, `pending_approval`) after full server-side re-validation, then attempts immediate composition using the submitting actor's own identity — this succeeds synchronously (a real, literal "auto-approve inline" outcome, `status='fulfilled'` before the call even returns) only for a `discount_voucher` reward submitted by an actor who independently holds `LYL:Edit` (staff, or a future system caller); a genuine customer submission of ANY reward_type gracefully falls back to `pending_approval`, requiring one real, fast staff `app.decide_loyalty_redemption(approve)` call to complete the identical composition. **Live effect:** a fully autonomous, zero-staff-involvement instant self-service redemption does not exist for any reward_type from a raw customer session in this checkpoint — mirrors the already-established "on-demand/staff-triggered only" precedent family (`ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`/`129`) this Loyalty domain has consistently disclosed at every prior checkpoint, extended here to this domain's own last remaining synchronous-composition gap. The full reasoning (including a live-tested confirmation that `auth.uid()` is unaffected by nested `SECURITY DEFINER` calls, which is why the identity crosscheck alone cannot solve this) is recorded in the migration's own design decision 5.

**Item 2 — discount_voucher entitlement `value_amount`/`currency` are sourced from the reward's own staff-only `internal_cost` and the tenant's own resolved `default_currency` (`app.resolve_tenant_locale`, PLT), a genuinely new composition, not a claimed reuse.** CPL-320's own `app.loyalty_rewards` has no dedicated customer-facing monetary "voucher face value" column, yet `app.issue_loyalty_benefit_entitlement` (CPL-319) requires a real, positive `value_amount` and a real currency for every benefit_type, voucher included. A discount_voucher reward with a null or non-positive `internal_cost` is genuinely not configured for redemption and is rejected with a distinct, customer-safe error (`reward_redemption_unavailable`) rather than fabricating a value — proven live via this checkpoint's own adversarial atomicity db-test (a misconfigured voucher reward with real finite stock and a real points cost rolls back every prior composition step, including the redemption row's own `INSERT`).

**Item 3 — no notification/retry/DLQ mechanism.** The source prompt's own §20 asks for "notification, reversal, retry and DLQ handling." This checkpoint builds real, complete reversal (rejection/cancellation/fulfillment-failure all genuinely release stock and credit points back, live-proven adversarially) but no customer/staff notification on decision, and no automated retry/dead-letter handling for a failed downstream composition step — a staff member must notice a `pending_approval`/`fulfilling` queue item manually via the admin workbench this checkpoint builds. Mirrors the established "on-demand/staff-triggered only" precedent family exactly.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 is a real, necessary, and fully disclosed architectural resolution of a genuine RBAC/ADR-0024 Part B tension this checkpoint is the first Loyalty capability to encounter (no prior checkpoint composed a staff-only primitive from a customer-initiated flow); item 2 is a disclosed, necessary modeling decision closing a real gap in CPL-320's own schema; item 3 mirrors an already-accepted repository-wide-shaped precedent (`ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`/`129`). **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including a live-proven two-process concurrent stock race, a live-proven adversarial atomicity rollback, and a live-proven NULL-bypass optimistic-concurrency regression fix on `app.decide_loyalty_redemption`; no existing caller or test is affected; the business impact is operational latency for a genuine self-service auto-approve-eligible redemption, never incorrect state). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, a dedicated, cross-cutting, per-tenant "system/automation identity" provisioning capability (its own design decision, well beyond one capability prompt), after which `app.submit_loyalty_redemption`'s own composition attempt could use that identity instead of the raw customer's own; item 2, none required unless a future capability adds a dedicated customer-facing voucher face-value column to `app.loyalty_rewards`; item 3, a dedicated notification/job-queue capability wiring a real notification on every `app.loyalty_redemption_events` insert, and a retry/DLQ wrapper around `app._compose_loyalty_redemption_decision`'s own failure paths.

### ISS-2026-133 — Expiry and Fraud Prevention (CPL-322): self-approval not structurally blocked for the same staff member opening AND deciding a case; entitlement-level fraud hold not built; expiry sweep is on-demand/staff-triggered only (Phase 8, Batch 5, `CG-S13-CPL-024`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-18` at `CG-S13-CPL-024` (Prompt 322, Expiry and Fraud Prevention, the third prompt of Batch 5) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801240000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_expiry_fraud_prevention.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — self-approval is NOT structurally blocked between `app.open_loyalty_fraud_review_case` and `app.decide_loyalty_fraud_review_case`.** Every other maker-checker pair in this repository (PRC-264's own vendor-KPI precedent, CPL-318's own point-adjustment pair) blocks self-approval because the two roles are always two DIFFERENT humans (a maker requests, a DIFFERENT checker decides). This checkpoint's own pair is different in kind: the source prompt's own alternative flow frames it as SYSTEM/RULE (opens, provisional) vs. HUMAN REVIEWER (decides, final) — not two different humans — and no live rule/signal-detection engine exists anywhere in this repository (source prompt business rule: "predictive fraud depth remains Step 14") to open a case autonomously in this checkpoint. Every `open_loyalty_fraud_review_case` call today is therefore itself staff-initiated (`opened_by = p_actor_label`, a real staff actor's own label), and that SAME staff member deciding their own just-opened case is a real, narrow gap this checkpoint does not close. Both `app.open_loyalty_fraud_review_case` and `app.decide_loyalty_fraud_review_case` require the elevated `LYL:Configure` authority (design decision 4), so the gap is bounded to already-privileged actors, not any arbitrary caller.

**Item 2 — entitlement-level fraud hold (composing CPL-319's `app.hold_loyalty_benefit_entitlement`/`app.release_loyalty_benefit_entitlement_hold` for a single voucher/cashback/discount row) was not built; account-level coverage is disclosed as sufficient for this checkpoint.** Reasoning in full: (a) an account-level hold already blocks every redemption for the account (this checkpoint's own design decision 3) — any investigation broad enough to warrant halting activity is already fully covered; (b) CPL-319's own entitlement-hold primitives already exist, are already independently staff-callable (`LYL:Configure`) today via the already-shipped `admin/loyalty-benefits` UI, with zero new code needed for a staff member to hold ONE suspicious entitlement directly; (c) building a second, parallel case-and-decide review-case mechanism scoped to individual entitlements would meaningfully widen this migration's already-substantial scope with no concrete, disclosed business need calling for it at this checkpoint.

**Item 3 — `app.run_loyalty_expiry_sweep` is on-demand/staff-triggered only — no live scheduler exists anywhere in this repository (the same disclosed `NOT_RUN` class `PLT-123`/`125`/`132` and `HRT-289`/`291` already established, and the identical "on-demand/staff-triggered only" precedent family `ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`/`129`/`132` have each already disclosed for their own sibling Loyalty primitives).** A real, complete, idempotent, storm-controlled RPC exists and is live-proven under a genuine two-process concurrent race in this checkpoint's own db-test — only the periodic-invocation wiring is deferred.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 is a real, disclosed, narrow gap bounded to already-`LYL:Configure`-privileged actors, not a new class of unauthenticated/under-privileged access; item 2 is a deliberate, reasoned scope boundary, not an oversight; item 3 mirrors an already-accepted repository-wide-shaped precedent. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all three items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including a live-proven two-process concurrent storm-control race, live-proven optimistic-concurrency NULL-bypass regressions across `claim`/`decide`/`revoke`, a live cross-prompt regression proof that a held account is genuinely blocked from CPL-321's own `app.submit_loyalty_redemption`, and a grep-provable redaction guarantee that `risk_signal_type`/`risk_signal_detail`/`review_reason`/`reviewed_by` never reach any customer-facing read; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, if a real rule/signal-detection engine is ever built (Step 14), give it its own system-labeled `opened_by` distinct from any human `LYL:Configure` actor, then block a human from deciding a case they personally opened, mirroring PRC-264's own `requested_by_auth_user_id = p_actor_auth_user_id` check; item 2, build the entitlement-scoped variant only if a genuine future business need for a governed (not merely ad hoc) entitlement-level review workflow emerges; item 3, none required beyond a future scheduler wiring a periodic call to the already-real `app.run_loyalty_expiry_sweep`.

### ISS-2026-134 — Liability Reconciliation Analytics (CPL-323): reconciliation is currency-scoped (one run per currency for full multi-currency coverage) and reflects current state only (no point-in-time historical bound); a null `internal_cost` on an open reward-fulfillment redemption contributes 0 with no exception; engagement metrics/reconciliation runs are on-demand/staff-triggered only; no Finance-side liability handoff exists yet (Phase 8, Batch 5, `CG-S13-CPL-025`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered/disclosed `2026-08-18` at `CG-S13-CPL-025` (Prompt 323, Liability Reconciliation Analytics, the fourth and final prompt of Batch 5) — deliberate scope decisions made while authoring `supabase/migrations/20260801250000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_analytics.sql`, not defects found afterward.

**Item 1 — `app.execute_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_run` is CURRENCY-SCOPED via a required `p_currency` parameter (this checkpoint's own disclosed addition beyond the source prompt's own literal 4-parameter signature).** Cashback/discount/voucher liability totals only ever include entitlements whose own `currency` column matches the run's own currency — never blended into one fake cross-currency total (the identical "dimension by unit type, never force-sum" discipline this checkpoint's own points-liability design decision already applies to the points-to-currency question, applied a second time here). A tenant with genuinely multi-currency entitlements needs one run PER currency for full coverage — mirrors FIN-209's own per-scope (`ar`/`ap`) run precedent exactly, not a new pattern.

**Item 2 — `p_as_of` is recorded as a run's own point-in-time label but does NOT bound which raw ledger/event rows are included — every total is computed against the FULL CURRENT state of the source tables at execution time.** A true point-in-time historical reconciliation (bounding inclusion by `created_at <= as_of`, mirroring FIN-209's own `as_of_date`-bounded control/source totals) is not built: unlike FIN-209's own AR/AP open-item tables, `app.loyalty_point_balances`/`app.loyalty_benefit_entitlements` are both current-state-only with no historical-snapshot capability for any date other than "now" — attempting a historical bound would make this checkpoint's own exactness cross-check (comparing a live-recomputed total against the CURRENT cached balance/status column) structurally meaningless for any `as_of` genuinely in the past. Every run therefore reflects "now," regardless of the `as_of` value recorded on it.

**Item 3 — the reward-fulfillment-exposure liability line (`reward_fulfillment_liability_total`, valued at `app.loyalty_rewards.internal_cost` for open `physical_item`/`service_credit` redemptions) silently contributes 0 for a reward whose own `internal_cost` is null**, rather than raising a third exception type. `app.loyalty_rewards.internal_cost` is nullable at the schema level (CPL-320); a null value on an actively-fulfilling redemption is a real, if unlikely, staff data-entry gap this checkpoint does not separately flag.

**Item 4 — `app.execute_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_run`/`app.get_loyalty_engagement_metrics` are on-demand/staff-triggered only** — no live scheduler exists anywhere in this repository (the same disclosed `NOT_RUN` class `PLT-123`/`125`/`132`/`HRT-289`/`291` already established, and the identical "on-demand/staff-triggered only" precedent family `ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`/`129`/`132`/`133` have each already disclosed for their own sibling Loyalty primitives).

**Item 5 — no Finance-side liability-handoff mechanism (a handoff-batch table, an idempotent generator, a Finance acknowledgement RPC — the HRT-282-family shape ADR-0024 Part D names) is built.** This checkpoint's own migration header discloses this as a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight: no Finance-side liability-handoff contract exists anywhere in this repository for Loyalty to hand off TO yet, so fabricating one would be inventing a Finance-side contract Finance itself never asked for. This checkpoint instead builds a real, complete, certifiable liability-evidence layer entirely within Loyalty's own tables — closing `ISS-2026-129` item 1 on its own terms — that a future Finance-handoff checkpoint can read from.

**Not fixed here** — item 1 mirrors FIN-209's own already-accepted per-scope run precedent; item 2 is a real, structural bound (the source tables genuinely have no historical-snapshot capability), disclosed rather than silently narrowed; item 3 is a disclosed, low-likelihood data-entry gap, not a live defect; item 4 mirrors an already-accepted repository-wide-shaped precedent; item 5 is the identical, already-accepted "domain stays source of truth, Finance handoff is a later, separate step" discipline HRT-282 already established for Payroll. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity for all five items (no data fabricated or leaked; every RPC this checkpoint ships is real, complete, and correctly gated — including a live-proven forced-mismatch-produces-a-real-exception-row proof for both the point-balance and entitlement-state derivation checks, a live-proven certify-blocked-while-open-exceptions-remain gate, live-proven optimistic-concurrency NULL-bypass regressions on both `resolve`/`certify`, and a live-proven customer_user-caller-rejected-outright proof on engagement metrics; no existing caller or test is affected). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: item 1, none required unless a tenant genuinely needs one blended cross-currency total, which would require a real, configured currency-conversion source this repository does not have; item 2, a dedicated point-in-time ledger/event-log reconstruction capability, substantially more scope than this single checkpoint; item 3, a third exception type (e.g. `reward_internal_cost_missing`) if this gap is ever observed in practice; item 4, a dedicated scheduler capability wiring a periodic call to the already-real `app.execute_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_run`; item 5, the HRT-282-family Finance-handoff capability ADR-0024 Part D already names, once a real Finance-side liability contract exists to hand off to.

### ISS-2026-135 — a third `scripts/db-tests/*.sql` file (`hris-shift-roster-scheduling.sql`) confirmed to belong to the already-registered day-of-week/wall-clock-dependent fixture-flakiness class (`ISS-2026-077`/`103`/`115`) — encountered while re-running the FULL `pnpm run db:test` harness during Batch 5's own Tier C review (Phase 8, Batch 5 Tier C review, `CG-S13-CPL-022..025`, `RESOLVED` 2026-08-23 at `CG-S15-HDN-002`, was Low — pre-existing, unrelated to Batch 5, not fixed there)

Encountered `2026-08-18` (a Tuesday) while the Batch 5 Tier C review (`CPL-320..323`) fix pass re-ran the full `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` harness (200+ files) fresh, after fixing this batch's own `scripts/db-tests/customer-loyalty-liability-reconciliation.sql` UUID-range collision with `finance-cash-bank.sql`/`procurement-sourcing.sql` (see `CPL-323.md` §14) — that fix let the harness run substantially further than before (cleanly past both previously-colliding files), and it then halted at `scripts/db-tests/hris-shift-roster-scheduling.sql:1050`: `assertion failed: expected schedule_assignment_id to stay null when no roster assignment exists for this employee/work_date` — emp3, this fixture's own explicit negative control (deliberately given no roster assignment for "today"), unexpectedly carried a real, non-null `schedule_assignment_id` on a clock-in.

**Confirmed same class, not investigated further (out of this review's own Batch-5/Loyalty scope):** `hris-shift-roster-scheduling.sql` is 100% Phase 7 (HRIS) scope — zero Batch 5/Loyalty migration or db-test file references it, and no Batch 5 migration touches `app.schedule_assignments`/`app.set_schedule_coverage_requirement`/`app.assign_employee_schedule`/`app.attendance_sessions` at all (grep-confirmed). `ISS-2026-077`'s own already-registered root cause (`app.set_schedule_coverage_requirement`'s own `extract(dow from current_date)` call, several already-registered entries up, ties fixture-seeded schedule-coverage behavior to which day of the week the suite happens to run on) is the same general mechanism class this negative-control assertion is exposed to — a roster/coverage rule keyed to day-of-week can legitimately auto-generate a real assignment for a nominally-unscheduled employee on some days and not others, which is exactly what a fixture asserting an unconditional "always null" outcome cannot tolerate. This specific file/day combination was not previously enumerated by `ISS-2026-077`/`ISS-2026-103` (both of which name `hris-overtime-timesheet.sql`/`procurement-vendor-performance.sql`/`hris-leave-permit-business-trip.sql`, never this file), so it is registered here as its own entry per this document's own append-only, never-edit-an-existing-entry discipline (mirrors `ISS-2026-103`'s own precedent for naming additional files in the same already-established class, rather than editing `ISS-2026-077`'s own text).

**Not fixed here** — per `AGENTS.md`'s "fix only task-caused failures; log unrelated/pre-existing failures and create a separate recovery task" and per this review's own explicit charter (Batch 5, `CPL-320..323` only) — `scripts/db-tests/hris-shift-roster-scheduling.sql` is Phase 7/HRIS-owned scope, not touched by any Batch 5 migration. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (the underlying scheduling/attendance-linking logic is not shown to be wrong — only a test fixture's own negative-control assumption depends on the run day). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: identify the specific day-of-week-relative rule/fixture-seed step upstream of emp3's own assertion (mirrors this file's own already-known day-of-week coupling in its schedule-coverage-requirement setup) and pin it to a fixed reference day, or make the negative-control assertion itself day-of-week-independent, the same fix class every other entry in this cluster (`ISS-2026-077`/`103`/`115`) already recommends for its own file.


**RESOLVED 2026-08-23 at `CG-S15-HDN-002` (Prompt 370, Step 15 Full Regression).** Also misclassified: this is **not** a day-of-week defect and has no wall-clock coupling at all. `scripts/db-tests/hris-shift-roster-scheduling.sql` contains exactly one date-relative expression and it is already pinned to a literal; `git log --follow` confirms the file has not been touched since Prompt 295, i.e. before this issue was even registered, so no intervening fix could explain it either. The real mechanism: emp3 is given `bulk_generated` roster assignments on the **hardcoded literal dates** `2026-08-17` and `2026-08-18`, and the negative control then asserts `schedule_assignment_id IS NULL` for the real wall-clock work day. Swept across 30 candidate dates against live fixture state: the old assertion would fail on **exactly one — `2026-08-18`, a Tuesday**. It is a time bomb, not a flake, and "those dates are in the past" is not a fix: it re-arms the moment anyone refreshes the fixture's literal dates forward, which is ordinary maintenance. **Fixed** by deriving the expectation from real state and asserting in both directions — no published assignment for the session's work day means the link must be null; one that does exist means the session must link to exactly it. The property genuinely under test (decision 9: a clock-in never fabricates a roster link and never errors without one) is now strictly stronger and true on every calendar date. Evidence: `docs/build-log/full-system-hardening/HDN-370.md` §5.3/§8.

### ISS-2026-136 — Liability Reconciliation Analytics (CPL-323): `reward_fulfillment_liability_total` is NOT currency-scoped, unlike the other four liability lines, causing silent double-counting if a multi-currency tenant's per-currency reconciliation runs are summed as the migration's own design decision 6 instructs (Phase 8, CPL-324 Integrated Verification, `CG-S13-CPL-026`, `RESOLVED` 2026-08-20 — item 1 only, item 2 remains `OPEN`, Low)

Found `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-026` (Prompt 324, Customer Portal and Loyalty Integrated Verification) — the loyalty-ledger-reconciliation lens's live-reproduced report, independently re-derived and confirmed by direct code read (not accepted on the lens's word alone) before being registered here.

**Item 1 — the reward-fulfillment exposure loop inside `app.execute_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_run` (`supabase/migrations/20260801250000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_analytics.sql`, the loop starting around line 592) carries no `p_currency` predicate anywhere, unlike the cashback/discount/voucher loop directly above it (line ~560, which explicitly filters `and v_entitlement.currency = p_currency`).** Confirmed live: an identical tenant/instant, one `fulfilling` `physical_item` redemption with `internal_cost = 75`, produces `reward_fulfillment_liability_total = 75` on BOTH a USD-scoped run and an IDR-scoped run of the same tenant — both certify cleanly with zero exceptions. This migration's own design decision 6 (and `ISS-2026-134` item 1's own existing text) tells operators to run reconciliation "once per currency... for full coverage" of a multi-currency tenant — the DOCUMENTED, intended usage pattern for every other liability line. Following that exact documented workflow and summing the four other lines' own per-currency totals is correct; doing the same for `reward_fulfillment_liability_total` silently overcounts it once per additional currency the tenant has an open `fulfilling` redemption in, with no exception ever raised (the cross-check machinery in design decisions 7/8 only compares a run's own cached-vs-derived status, never a cross-run/cross-currency consistency).

**Item 2 (lower severity, folded into this same entry rather than a separate number) — mismatch DETECTION for entitlements/redemptions is tenant-wide, not currency-scoped, so one corrupted row is re-flagged as an open exception on every currency-scoped run, not only the run in its own currency.** Confirmed live: a USD-only cashback entitlement's corrupted status also appears as an open `entitlement_state_derivation_mismatch` exception on a same-tenant IDR-scoped run. This never produces a wrong liability NUMBER (only item 1 does that) — it only means the identical underlying data-quality defect must be independently `resolve`d once per currency-scoped run before each such run can `certify`, real but bounded operational noise, arguably defensible as "tenant-wide derivation-exactness assurance" rather than a bug in its own right.

**Root cause (item 1):** `app.loyalty_rewards` has no currency column of its own (`design decision 1`'s own already-disclosed "tenant-default-currency assumption" for `internal_cost`) — there is no `reward.currency` value to compare against `p_currency` even if the predicate were added naively. A correct fix requires a real currency-modeling decision, not a one-line predicate: either (a) add a `currency` column to `app.loyalty_rewards` (a schema change — genuinely new capability surface, not available to this bounded verification checkpoint's own "no planned feature schema except minimal registered defect repair" charter), or (b) keep the total intentionally currency-UNSCOPED but change its own reporting contract (return it only once, tagged as tenant-wide, never inside a per-currency breakdown) and update every consumer (the RPC's own return shape, `server/queries`/`server/mutations` wrappers, admin UI, and this migration's own design decision 6/`ISS-2026-134` text) to match — also beyond "minimal" for this checkpoint.

**Escalation check (per this checkpoint's own instruction to escalate any cross-tenant/cross-account leakage, balance/liability manipulation, or double-spend finding to Critical regardless of original label): considered and NOT escalated.** No tenant/account boundary is crossed (the bug reproduces within a single tenant's own two currency-scoped runs); no customer balance, points, entitlement, or redemption row is manipulated, corrupted, or double-spent (every OTHER liability line, and every underlying ledger/entitlement/redemption row, stays exactly correct — live-reproduced across five independent forced-corruption scenarios this same checkpoint, all caught correctly); each INDIVIDUAL run's own reported number is accurate for its own query, self-consistently. The live, reachable failure mode is narrower: a staff member manually summing this one line across multiple per-currency runs (following the migration's own documented multi-run workflow) gets an inflated total. No automated Finance-side liability-handoff consumer exists yet to propagate this automatically (`ISS-2026-129` item 5, independently reconfirmed still accurate this same checkpoint) — today's blast radius is a manual reporting step, not a live financial commitment. High severity (not Critical) is the honest rating: real, live-reproduced, reachable via the migration's own documented intended workflow, and material to the "certified == trustworthy" guarantee this checkpoint's own header names as the reconciliation artifact's central purpose — but not a security, tenancy, or ledger-correctness breach.

**Not fixed at CPL-324's own close** — both items were assessed as requiring a currency-modeling design decision (schema addition or reporting-contract change) exceeding that verification-only checkpoint's own bounded "minimal registered defect repair" authority.

**Item 1 `RESOLVED` (2026-08-20, orchestrating session, immediately following CPL-324's own close, before advancing to CPL-325 — the source spec's own literal acceptance criterion, "No unresolved critical/high blocker may advance," required resolving this before Batch 5's closure sequence could continue).** Option (b) from the root-cause analysis above was selected: `app.loyalty_rewards`' own `internal_cost` is now explicitly treated as denominated in the tenant's own resolved `default_currency` (`app.resolve_tenant_locale`, PLT) — the SAME already-established resolution this exact repository already uses for an identical "no currency column" value at `app.issue_loyalty_benefit_entitlement`'s own discount_voucher-redemption call site (CPL-321 design decision 4) — rather than inventing a new column or a new convention. `supabase/migrations/20260801270000_harden_customer_portal_loyalty_liability_reward_fulfillment_currency_scope.sql` (`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` against `app.execute_loyalty_liability_reconciliation_run` only, the already-applied `20260801250000` migration file untouched) adds one resolved `v_tenant_default_currency` lookup and one additional predicate (`and p_currency = v_tenant_default_currency`) to the reward-fulfillment loop's own existing accumulation condition — every other line is byte-identical to the prior body. Live-reproduced, fixed: `scripts/db-tests/customer-loyalty-liability-reconciliation.sql` gained a new mandatory regression block reproducing this item's own exact two-currency scenario (a USD-denominated tenant's IDR-scoped run now correctly reports `reward_fulfillment_liability_total = 0`, while a same-instant USD-scoped run still correctly reports `75`) plus a small fixture addition (a real published `USD` tenant locale for the test's own tenant, making its own long-standing implicit USD assumption explicit) — run clean on 5 independent fresh (drop+recreate) scratch-database runs. Full `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` re-run clean after this fix (see `docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-324.md` §"Verdict" addendum).

**Item 2 remains `OPEN`, Low** — unchanged from the original text above; not touched by this fix (a separate, lower-severity, disclosed-as-acceptable operational-noise characteristic, not a wrong-number defect).

### ISS-2026-137 — `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` carries the identical Supreme-Admin-override gap `ISS-2026-130` closed for its own 5-table scope, but was not itself included in that fix (Phase 8, CPL-325, `CG-S13-CPL-027`, OPEN, Low)

Discovered `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-027` (Prompt 325, Customer Portal and Loyalty Privacy Integrity Hardening) while ruling on `ISS-2026-130`. `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` (CPL-317, `supabase/migrations/20260801190000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_membership_tier.sql`) was named in `ISS-2026-130`'s own ORIGINAL four-table list (Batch 4, before `CPL-320`/`CPL-321` existed) but this checkpoint's own explicit remediation scope named a different 5-table set instead — the original three still-relevant tables plus the two newer Batch-5 append-only tables that postdate `ISS-2026-130`'s own original disclosure (`app.loyalty_reward_stock_reservations`, `app.loyalty_redemption_events`) — omitting `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` itself.

Grep-confirmed: `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements` still grants only `select, insert` to `service_role` (`20260801190000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_membership_tier.sql:1192`), zero `UPDATE`/`DELETE` to any role, staff or Supreme Admin alike — the identical gap `ISS-2026-130` closed for its own 5 tables. The same mitigating reasoning applies unchanged: the absence makes this ledger MORE immutable, not less secure — no live vulnerability, only a missing disclosed correction path.

**Not fixed here** — outside this checkpoint's own explicitly authorized 5-table scope (adding a 6th table was not part of the authorized remediation and would exceed "minimal registered defect repair" without an explicit scope grant to do so). **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (mirrors `ISS-2026-130`'s own original Medium-then-resolved shape, downgraded to Low here since the fix pattern is now proven, tested, and trivially extensible — closing this is a small, bounded, well-understood follow-up, not new design work). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint picks this up: extend `app.protect_loyalty_ledger_append_only()` (already generic, keyed off `TG_TABLE_NAME`/`OLD.tenant_id`/`OLD.id`, no table-specific logic) with one more `create trigger ... before update or delete on app.loyalty_account_tier_movements ... execute function app.protect_loyalty_ledger_append_only();` plus the matching `grant update, delete on app.loyalty_account_tier_movements to service_role;` — a single additive migration, mirroring `supabase/migrations/20260801280000_harden_customer_portal_loyalty_ledger_supreme_admin_override.sql` exactly.

### ISS-2026-138 — RPD-023 (MFA/step-up-authorization) disclosure practice was silently dropped for CPL-316–323 (all of Loyalty, including reward approval and fraud release, the two categories this repository's own hardening charter names by name), and CPL-315's own `ISS-2026-125` falsely cites a CPL-314 disclosure that does not exist (Phase 8, CPL-325, `CG-S13-CPL-027`, Medium, OPEN)

Discovered `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-027` (Prompt 325, Customer Portal and Loyalty Privacy Integrity Hardening), verified directly against every Phase 8 build log rather than accepted from any prior batch's own claim: `grep -ic "RPD-023\|MFA\|step-up"` against `docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-3NN.md` for every capability returns 1-4 hits for CPL-300 through CPL-313 and CPL-315, but **exactly 0 hits for CPL-314 and for every one of CPL-316 through CPL-323** — the entire back half of Phase 8, including reward approval (CPL-320/321) and fraud release (CPL-322), the exact two high-risk action categories source spec §20 item 4 names explicitly as needing MFA/current-auth/RPD-022 disclosure. No Phase 8 migration SQL file cites RPD-023 either.

Compounding this, `ISS-2026-125` (registered at CPL-315, above) states the underlying MFA gap is "already disclosed identically at CPL-300 §9 and CPL-314" — `docs/build-log/phase-08/CPL-314.md` contains **zero** mentions of MFA/RPD-023/step-up in any form, grep-confirmed. This is the same citation-accuracy defect class Batch 4's own Tier C review already found and fixed once (a mischaracterized `06_RLS_RBAC_WORKSTREAM.md` §8 quote, CPL-318) — here it recurred in the same batch at CPL-315, and the underlying disclosure practice itself was then dropped entirely for the remainder of Phase 8 rather than merely mis-cited once.

The underlying fact this practice discloses remains true and is NOT itself a new finding — RPD-023/MFA has never been built anywhere in this repository (a standing, pre-existing, repository-wide gap, consistently and accurately disclosed at CPL-300/301/302/303/304/306/307/308/309/310/311/312/313/315); `app.assert_actor_is_session_identity` (the "current-auth" half of RPD-023) IS real and is the literal first statement in every privileged RPC checked this checkpoint (redemption decide, fraud-case decide, liability certify, profile-change decide), zero exceptions found. What is new here is narrower and specifically about **disclosure completeness and citation accuracy**, not about the underlying MFA gap itself.

**Not fixed here** — a doc-only correction, bounded and additive in shape, but this checkpoint's own hardening lenses were instructed not to edit `docs/runtime/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` directly from inside a no-repo-edit lens; the orchestrating CPL-325 session registers this issue in that lens's place. **Status `OPEN`**, Medium (a real, live disclosure-completeness gap against a source-spec-named requirement — RPD-023 for reward approval/fraud release specifically — not merely a citation nit, though the citation error itself is a contributing, correctable component). Recommended fix for whichever future checkpoint or documentation pass (CPL-326 Documentation/Handoff is the natural owner) picks this up: (a) correct `ISS-2026-125`'s own false CPL-314 citation in place (do not delete — this entry's own governing convention, item 1 below, forbids that) by appending a note here pointing to this correction; (b) add one line to CPL-314's and CPL-316 through CPL-323's own build logs (or a single consolidated forward-pointing note in this file, mirroring how `ISS-2026-126`/`127`/`128`/`129`'s own "on-demand/staff-triggered only" precedent family is cited by name rather than re-derived at each site) confirming the RPD-023 gap remains open and applies to reward approval/fraud release specifically, per source spec §20 item 4 and §24 RPD-023's own literal text ("MFA/current authorization for privileged customer-admin, reward approval, export and support actions").

### ISS-2026-139 — Redemption Approval and Fulfillment (CPL-321): a staff actor holding only `LYL:Edit` (not `LYL:Configure`) can submit AND instantly auto-fulfill a `discount_voucher` redemption for ANY loyalty account in the tenant, in one call — collapsing maker and checker into a single, lower-privileged actor and bypassing the `LYL:Configure`-gated `app.decide_loyalty_redemption` governance path entirely (Phase 8, CPL-325, `CG-S13-CPL-027`, Medium, OPEN)

Discovered/live-reproduced `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-027` (Prompt 325, Customer Portal and Loyalty Privacy Integrity Hardening). A staff actor holding only `LYL:Edit` (not `LYL:Configure`) calling `app.submit_loyalty_redemption` for a `discount_voucher` reward against ANY loyalty account in the tenant — including one with no relationship to the caller's own identity — reaches `status=fulfilled` inside the single `submit` call: stock reserved, points consumed, entitlement issued, with `app.decide_loyalty_redemption` (the `LYL:Configure`-gated approval RPC this repository elsewhere consistently treats as the governance checkpoint for a redemption decision) never invoked at all.

**Root cause** (`supabase/migrations/20260801230000_create_customer_portal_loyalty_redemption_approval_fulfillment.sql`): the standing scope check (`if not v_is_staff and array_length(v_scope,1) is null then raise ...`) treats bare `LYL:Edit` (`v_is_staff`) as sufficient to bypass the customer-account-scope check entirely, so a staff actor may name any account in the tenant. The submit-time auto-compose branch for `discount_voucher` then composes inline whenever the submitter independently holds `LYL:Edit` — with no separate decide step, and no check that the submitter is deciding someone ELSE's request, because there is no decide step on this path at all.

This is deliberate, tested, documented behavior — `scripts/db-tests/customer-loyalty-redemption.sql`'s own "main flow A" exercises this exact shape and asserts it as intended, and it is disclosed under `ISS-2026-132` item 1 — but that disclosure frames the mechanism entirely as a UX/availability rationale ("why a genuine customer_user cannot get instant self-service") and never flags the DIFFERENT angle this entry discloses: the same mechanism lets one lower-privileged (`Edit`, not `Configure`) staff actor collapse maker and checker into a single call for an arbitrary account. Every other Loyalty maker-checker pair in this repository (point adjustment — `app.decide_loyalty_point_adjustment`, self-approval structurally blocked; customer profile-change — `app.decide_customer_profile_change_request`, self-approval structurally blocked) enforces a hard two-actor rule even among already-privileged staff; this is the one exception, and it requires a LOWER privilege tier (`Edit`) than the governance action (`Configure`-gated decide) it substitutes for.

**Escalation check applied** (this checkpoint's own instruction: cross-tenant/cross-account leak, balance/liability manipulation, or double-spend → Critical regardless of original label): does not meet that bar — single tenant, real (not corrupted) points/stock/entitlement accounting throughout, and the actor already holds a real, elevated, granted `LYL:Edit` authority (not an unprivileged or forged identity). Rated Medium: a real governance-control gap reachable by a real granted role, not a live security breach.

**Not fixed here** — changing this would mean removing or gating an intentional, already-tested, already-asserted design decision (`scripts/db-tests/customer-loyalty-redemption.sql`'s own "main flow A"), which is a policy/RBAC decision exceeding this checkpoint's own "minimal registered defect repair" authority, not a bounded code defect with one clear correct answer. **Status `OPEN`**, Medium. Recommended resolution path for whichever future checkpoint picks this up (a deliberate governance decision, not a mechanical fix): either (a) require `LYL:Configure` (not `LYL:Edit`) for the submit-time auto-compose branch specifically, closing the privilege-tier mismatch while leaving the graceful `pending_approval` fallback unchanged for every other caller, or (b) keep `LYL:Edit` sufficient but add a maker/checker identity check (submitter auth_user_id must differ from a configured elevated actor, mirroring `app.decide_loyalty_point_adjustment`'s own `self_approval_not_allowed` pattern) — either requires a real product decision about the intended governance model for this specific path, not a unilateral migration.

### ISS-2026-140 — zero automated accessibility-audit evidence exists for any of Phase 8's ~30 Customer Portal routes or 9 admin Loyalty routes (Phase 8, CPL-326, `CG-S13-CPL-028`, Medium for the Customer Portal half / Low for the admin-Loyalty half, OPEN)

Discovered `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-028` (Prompt 326, Customer Portal and Loyalty Documentation Handoff), UX/accessibility/performance lens, independently re-verified this checkpoint rather than accepted from the lens's own word alone.

**What exists, confirmed real.** A genuine, wired Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` accessibility harness exists (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`, `e2e/tenant-admin-portal.spec.ts`, `e2e/vendor-registration.spec.ts`, `e2e/supreme-admin-portal.spec.ts`), running in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `e2e` job, `pnpm run test:e2e`, established at `CG-S5-PH0-012`/Prompt 91, ADR-0007/ADR-0008). `new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()` is genuinely invoked — but only against synthetic inline HTML fixtures (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`) and two unrelated public, unauthenticated routes (`/login` in `e2e/tenant-admin-portal.spec.ts`; `/vendor-intake/*` in `e2e/vendor-registration.spec.ts`). `e2e/supreme-admin-portal.spec.ts` only asserts an unauthenticated redirect to `/login`, no axe scan. Independently re-confirmed this checkpoint: zero `.spec.ts` file anywhere in `e2e/` navigates to any `customer-*`/`customer-loyalty*` route or any `admin/loyalty*` route, and zero axe scan has ever run against any of them.

**Root cause: no live Supabase project exists in this sandbox.** Every Customer Portal route sits behind `lib/portal/customer-portal-guard.ts`'s own real, live-status-checking auth guard (CPL-300) — reaching any of the ~30 Customer Portal routes or 9 admin Loyalty routes with a real Playwright browser session requires a real authenticated session, which requires a real Supabase auth backend. This is a repository-wide constraint (no route behind any tenant/customer auth guard, in any phase, has ever been reached by a live e2e run in this repository's own history), not something Phase 8 introduced or could have fixed within its own bounded scope.

**Source-level evidence of accessible intent exists** (not a substitute for a run audit, but relevant context): `role="alert"`/`role="status"` on live-region feedback, `aria-current="page"` on the nav (`components/domain/customer-portal-nav.tsx`), `label`/`htmlFor` pairing on form fields, and status communicated via text/icon rather than color alone, spot-checked directly across several Customer Portal and admin Loyalty routes this checkpoint. None of this has been machine-verified by an actual accessibility audit against a live rendered page for either the Customer Portal or the admin Loyalty surface.

**Not fixed here** — building or wiring a live Supabase auth backend into this sandbox so `e2e/*.spec.ts` can reach an authenticated route is a repository-wide test-infrastructure capability, not a bounded documentation-checkpoint defect repair, and is explicitly out of `CG-S13-CPL-028`'s own "no planned feature schema except minimal registered defect repair" authority (source spec §13). **Status `OPEN`.** Severity: Medium for the Customer Portal half (~30 customer-facing routes, a real accessibility/WCAG compliance claim gap against RPD-024 with zero run evidence either way); Low for the admin-Loyalty half (9 internal staff-facing routes, lower external-accessibility-exposure risk, same zero-evidence gap). Owner: a future e2e-environment-enablement task (the root cause is a repository-wide constraint outside this checkpoint's authority to fix) that stands up a real or seeded Supabase auth backend reachable from Playwright, then widens `e2e/*.spec.ts` to navigate and axe-scan a representative sample of Customer Portal and admin Loyalty routes per authenticated role.

**Widened (`HDN-380`): the root cause above is now precisely diagnosed, not just named.** This sandbox's own nested Docker daemon *can* pull every Supabase image and boot Postgres cleanly (all 328 migrations apply without error) — the actual failure is narrower than "no live Supabase project exists": every non-Postgres Supabase service container (auth/gateway/storage) fails to start with a specific, reproducible error, `runc create failed: ... error setting rlimit type 7: operation not permitted` — a `RLIMIT_NOFILE` container-runtime privilege this sandbox's Docker daemon does not grant to non-Postgres containers. This is the concrete, actionable blocker a future environment-enablement task needs to resolve (a container-runtime privilege grant or an alternative to the bundled `supabase start` stack), not an open-ended "stand up Supabase somehow." **Interim mitigation partially landed this checkpoint**: `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`'s `recommended` rule set is now wired into `eslint.config.js` (`HDN-380`, see `HDN-380.md`) and running repository-wide — it catches unlabeled form controls and several other static a11y defect classes without a live backend, though (confirmed directly, not assumed) it does not catch color-contrast failures, missing landmark/`<main>` structure (`ISS-2026-241`), or `aria-invalid`/field-level error association (`ISS-2026-242`) — a real rendered-page/axe audit against a live authenticated session, blocked by the rlimit issue above, remains the only way to close this entry fully.

### ISS-2026-141 — zero load/performance-test evidence exists for any Phase 8 route or RPC at declared target volume (Phase 8, CPL-326, `CG-S13-CPL-028`, Medium, OPEN)

Discovered `2026-08-20` at `CG-S13-CPL-028` (Prompt 326, Customer Portal and Loyalty Documentation Handoff), UX/accessibility/performance lens, independently re-verified this checkpoint rather than accepted from the lens's own word alone.

Discovered `2026-08-20` during Phase 8's own final closure checkpoint (`CG-S13-CPL-029`, Prompt 327), cross-cutting-compliance lens (RPD-025 sub-finding "NEW-1"), independently re-confirmed by this synthesis pass firsthand — not accepted on the lens's own word alone.

Zero Phase 8 table anywhere carries either column — independently re-confirmed by direct migration read, not merely the grep count.

`scripts/data-classification/registry.ts` (the repository's own canonical retention-class registry, `CG-S5-PH0-016`/Prompt 95) independently re-read in full this checkpoint: its `ClassificationEntry.id` values use exactly five domain prefixes — `env:`, `fin:`, `hrs:`, `prc:`, `tkt:` — confirmed by extracting and de-duplicating every `id:` literal in the file. **Zero `cpl:`/`lyl:`-prefixed entry exists**, and no `CUSTOMER_PORTAL_REGISTRY`/`LOYALTY_REGISTRY` export exists in the file at all (only `PHASE_0_REGISTRY`, `FINANCE_REGISTRY`, `PROCUREMENT_REGISTRY`, `HRS_REGISTRY`, `PAYROLL_REGISTRY`, `PERFORMANCE_REGISTRY`, `TRAINING_REGISTRY`, `TICKETING_REGISTRY`) — Phase 8 was never registered in this file at any point across all 29 of its own capability/hardening/documentation checkpoints.

This gap spans every new Phase 8 structured-data table with no upstream retention mechanism of its own: the 6 append-only Loyalty ledger tables (`app.loyalty_earning_events`, `app.loyalty_point_ledger_entries`, `app.loyalty_benefit_entitlement_events`, `app.loyalty_reward_stock_reservations`, `app.loyalty_redemption_events`, `app.loyalty_account_tier_movements`) plus every other new Phase 8 structured table (quote/booking request, shipment-order/tracking projection, profile change-request, loyalty program/tier-definition/reward-definition, redemption, liability-reconciliation-run tables, and siblings). **Files are explicitly out of scope for this entry** — portal document/invoice-support/ticket/reward-media attachments are fully covered by the pre-existing, structurally-enforced PLT-128 `app.files.retention_class`/`legal_hold` mechanism (source spec item 34's file half independently re-confirmed `PROVEN` this same checkpoint); this entry concerns only the structured relational rows those files' own metadata sits alongside, not the files themselves.

**Disposition:** Narrow blast radius — no live data leak, no access-control gap, and RPD-022/025's own governing rule is itself explicit that CargoGrid must never claim audit/retention records are tamper-proof or complete, so the honest posture is disclosure, not a false completeness claim. This is the **identical defect shape**, one phase later, as `ISS-2026-091` (Phase 7 HR/payroll structured-data tables, `HRT-293`, `CG-S12-HRT-021`): both describe real structured tables carrying zero `retention_class`/`legal_hold` column, both confirmed by the same "repository-wide grep across the phase's own migration range returns zero hits" method, both scoped to tables outside the two generic Platform primitives (`app.audit_logs`, `app.files`) that already carry this metadata, and both correctly disclosed rather than silently dropped or force-built outside a verification checkpoint's own bounded authority. `ISS-2026-091` was disclosed, non-blocking, at `PHASE_7_VERIFIED` closure (`docs/build-log/phase-07/HRIS_TICKETING_CLOSURE_REPORT.md` §3 item 34: "GAP, disclosed, non-blocking"; §19: "No live data leak; RPD-022 already requires disclosure over false completeness claims") and remains `OPEN` today, unfixed one phase later — this entry is registered on the identical precedent, not a novel one invented for this checkpoint.

**Not fixed by this checkpoint** — `CG-S13-CPL-029` is a closure-verification checkpoint with no planned-feature-schema authority (source spec's own charter is independent re-verification, not new migration work); adding real `retention_class`/`legal_hold`/`legal_hold_reason` columns (plus a purge/hold-enforcement mechanism that would actually act on them) across every Phase 8 structured table, deciding which retention class applies to which table family (ledger rows plausibly warrant the registry's own `audit_security_7y` class given their append-only/audit-adjacent nature, but quote/booking/profile-change-request tables need their own considered mapping, not a copy-paste default), and adding the corresponding `cpl:`/`lyl:` entries to `scripts/data-classification/registry.ts` is a genuine, multi-table, cross-cutting schema addition requiring its own design decision — not a bounded closure-checkpoint fix. **Status `OPEN`**, Medium severity (per this repository's own standing disposition rule, most recently applied at `ISS-2026-091`'s own Phase 7 closure: a confirmed Medium finding outside a verification checkpoint's own bounded authority is disclosed, not silently dropped, and does not by itself block a `_VERIFIED` closure state when no Critical/High finding accompanies it) — owner: a dedicated future cross-cutting retention-classification follow-up task, scoped to "add real `retention_class`/`legal_hold` columns, an enforcement mechanism, and matching `scripts/data-classification/registry.ts` `cpl:`/`lyl:` entries across every Phase 8 Customer Portal/Loyalty structured-data table at once," mirroring both `ISS-2026-091`'s own recommended fix shape and how `ISS-2026-027` (the analogous Phase 5 GPS-telemetry retention gap) was eventually closed for real, one phase later, rather than piecemeal per capability.

### ISS-2026-144 — `scripts/db-tests/procurement-vendor-performance.sql:978` intermittently fails a pre-existing Phase 6 assertion (New Vendor sparse-data `rate_validity` expected computable) (Phase 6, Procurement/Vendor Performance, pre-existing, confirmed flaky same-day, `OPEN`, Low)

Surfaced while establishing the mandatory fresh baseline for Phase 9's own kickoff (`CG-S14-IAE-001`, Prompt 329) — `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` halted (by design, `set -euo pipefail`) at `scripts/db-tests/procurement-vendor-performance.sql:978`: `assertion failed: expected New Vendor rate_validity to be computable (a real 0%, not a missing-data case)`. This file's own header (lines 9-13) documents that its fixtures are deliberately anchored to `now()` rather than a fixed calendar date specifically to avoid the day-of-week/date-dependent fixture-flakiness class already registered at `ISS-2026-077`/`103`/`115`/`135` — so this failure is not yet confirmed to be a member of that same known class; it may instead be a genuine, previously-undetected defect in the `rate_validity` computability rule for a vendor with zero contract/capacity/comparison history (the "New Vendor, sparse data" scenario). Verified by ad hoc re-run excluding only this one file (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/run-db-tests-skip-one.sh`, not committed, session-scratchpad only, this checkpoint): the remaining 193 of 194 files pass clean, `ALL PASSED`. Phase 6 (Procurement and Vendor Management) is already `PHASE_6_VERIFIED` (closed 2026-08-07) — this capability's own migrations are untouched by Phase 9's kickoff (zero migration/schema/RPC file written this checkpoint; independently re-confirmed by `git status --short` before this entry was written).

**Update (`CG-S14-IAE-006`, Prompt 334, same calendar day):** confirmed non-deterministic WITHIN the same day, not merely across days. Across 6 full `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` runs during Batch 1 (`IAE-002`..`IAE-006`), this exact assertion failed on 4 runs and passed cleanly (`ALL PASSED`, including this same file) on the 6th (`IAE-006`'s own final verification run) — no code touching this file's own migration or fixture changed between runs. This is real, load-bearing evidence of intra-day flakiness, not merely the unconfirmed cross-day question the entry originally posed; it does not yet pinpoint WHICH `now()`-anchored computation flips (candidate: a boundary condition in `rate_validity`'s own zero-history/sparse-data branch sensitive to sub-second or minute-level timing, not full calendar-day rollover). **Status `OPEN`**, re-triaged Medium → **Low** severity (the "genuine defect vs. flaky fixture" uncertainty the original entry reserved Medium for is now resolved in favor of flaky — a real product defect would not intermittently pass) — owner unchanged: a dedicated future Procurement/Vendor KPI recovery task, now scoped more precisely to (a) find the specific `now()`-relative boundary in `app.calculate_vendor_kpi_metrics`'s own `rate_validity` category logic that flips pass/fail run-to-run, and (b) widen or remove that boundary's sensitivity. Not fixed here per `AGENTS.md` "fix only task-caused failures... log unrelated/pre-existing failures and create a separate recovery task" — this is Phase-6-owned capability scope, not Phase 9.

### ISS-2026-145 — `scripts/db-tests/rbac-enforcement.sql`'s ATW-032/ISS-2026-032 actor-identity call-graph sweep now takes 15-20+ minutes standalone against the current ~2,398-function `app` schema (Phase 9, `CG-S14-IAE-002`, Prompt 330, `RESOLVED` at `HDN-379`, Low)

Surfaced while verifying `IAE-002` (Reporting Engine, Prompt 330): the repeated `AGENTS.md` Tier A requirement to run the full `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` (or an equivalent full suite) before every prompt's own commit now costs materially more wall-clock time than in earlier phases, driven almost entirely by one file. `scripts/db-tests/rbac-enforcement.sql`'s ATW-032 (`ISS-2026-032`) check builds a `fn`/`edge` recursive CTE that self-joins every function in the `app` schema against every other function with a regex match against each one's own `pg_get_functiondef` output (`select ... from fn c join fn e on c.oid <> e.oid where c.def ~ (...)`) — an O(n²) operation. Confirmed live this checkpoint: with 2,398 functions currently in `app` (`select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'app' and p.prokind = 'f'`), the file's own `ATW-032 (ISS-2026-032)` block alone measured 15-20+ minutes of active CPU time (`pg_stat_activity` confirmed `state = 'active'`, no `wait_event`, not a lock/hang) across two independent runs this checkpoint. This is a pre-existing condition, not something Prompt 330 introduced — the query shape is unchanged from whenever ATW-032 first added it; only the function count (which grows every phase) has crossed a threshold where the quadratic cost becomes materially noticeable. Every future Phase 9 capability prompt's own Tier A gate will pay this same, further-growing cost. **Status `OPEN`**, Low severity (correctness is unaffected — the check still runs to completion and still correctly catches real actor-identity gaps, as it did this same checkpoint; this is a build-velocity/test-infrastructure cost, not a product defect) — owner: a dedicated future test-infrastructure task, scoped to rewriting the `edge` CTE's self-join to a cheaper shape (e.g. a one-pass text-search index over each function's own `def`, or restricting the candidate set before the cross join) without weakening what the check actually proves. Not fixed here — rewriting a shared, security-relevant regression guard is outside a single capability prompt's own bounded scope, and `AGENTS.md`'s own execution-cadence discipline reserves broad refactors for a dedicated task.

**`RESOLVED` at `HDN-379`** (Prompt 379, Performance and Scalability, matrix §10 item 1). Rewrote the `edge` CTE from an `fn c join fn e on c.oid <> e.oid where c.def ~ (...)` self-join (one regex evaluation per PAIR, ~2,700² pairs at current scale) to a one-pass `fn f, regexp_matches(f.def, 'app\.([a-z0-9_]+)\s*\(', 'g') m` extraction (one regex evaluation per FUNCTION, joined afterward) — mirroring the identical technique already used, unmodified, in this same file's own sibling ATW-032/ISS-2026-033 block. Only edge construction changed; the `covered` recursive CTE's own multi-hop transitive-closure walk (a function that calls a helper that calls another helper that finally reaches `evaluate_permission`/`assert_actor_is_session_identity`) is byte-identical to before, so the invariant proved is unchanged. **Live-verified with a same-schema matched-pair run** (both the original and the rewritten query executed in the same transaction, against one 2,700-function disposable database, no rebuild in between — deliberately avoiding the accept-on-faith risk a naive before/after comparison across two separate database builds would carry): original **692,092.8ms** (~11.5 minutes), rewrite **556.4ms**, verdicts byte-identical (both empty — no unguarded function on the fully-migrated schema), **1244× speedup**. Full 229-file `bash scripts/db-tests/run.sh` re-run clean, `ALL PASSED`, confirming no other file's own assumptions about this block broke. **Status `RESOLVED`** — the check itself is unweakened (same invariant, same transitive-coverage semantics, live-verified identical on real data) and now costs well under 1 second instead of 15-20+ minutes, removing the build-velocity tax this issue was opened to track.

**A real, live-confirmed structural weakening was found and fixed at Tier C (attack-surface adversarial testing lens), still `RESOLVED`.** The first-draft rewrite's regex dropped two properties the original self-join carried "for free": a leading `\m` word-boundary anchor (so `webapp.foo(` could not be mistaken for a call to `app.foo`), and a real join-against-`fn` requirement (so `insert into app.some_table (...)` could not be mistaken for a call to a function named after the table). Live-forced against the real 2,700-function schema: **876 spurious edges**, all traced to unindexed table names in `insert into app.<table> (...)` statements — zero of the 876 phantom callee names collided with any real function name, so the rewrite never actually produced a wrong verdict on the current schema, but a future function literally named after an existing table, or a call site shaped like `wordapp.<realname>(`, could have silently marked a caller "covered" with no test failure. Fixed by restoring both properties: the regex now anchors `\mapp\.` and the `where` clause adds `and m[1] in (select proname from fn)` (a hash semi-join against the already-materialized `fn` CTE, not a new cross join — confirmed the fix stays O(n), re-timed at **1.66 seconds**, still ~417× faster than the original). Live-reproduced with 3 scratch functions: a phantom `insert into app.<name> (...)` targeting a name that is NOT a real function correctly produces no edge; a comment containing `webapp.<realname>(` correctly produces no edge (confirmed by removing the anchor and showing the false match reappears); a real call correctly still produces its edge. Full 229-file suite re-run clean after the fix.

**Timing-precision correction (Tier C correctness re-derivation lens): the original "692,092.8ms / 1244×" figures are a real, honest, live measurement — not a fixed, universally-reproducible constant.** An independent same-schema matched-pair re-run (same methodology, same 2,700-function build, a separate disposable database) measured the original query at **212,105.6ms** (~3.5 minutes) and the rewrite at **676.8ms** — a **≈313×** speedup, verdicts still byte-identical. Both measurements are real and neither is wrong; the ~3× spread in the ORIGINAL query's own absolute cost across two independent runs (692s vs. 212s) reflects real contention/load variance in this shared sandbox at the moment each was measured, not a flaw in either methodology (the REWRITE's own cost stayed close both times: 556ms vs. 677ms). The qualitative conclusion is unaffected and independently reconfirmed twice: a real, massive (300×-1200×+), correctness-preserving speedup, not a precise fixed multiplier — cite "300×-1200×+" rather than a single number when this fix is referenced elsewhere.

### ISS-2026-146 — cross-tenant `tenant_id` disclosure via exception message text, confirmed repository-wide (2,087+ occurrences since Phase 6), reproduced live in Group 8 (Phase 9, Group 8 Tier C review, `CG-S14-IAE-032..035`, Prompts 360-363, `OPEN`, Low)

Found by Group 8's own Tier C review (security/RLS/tenant lens), live-reproduced against a real disposable database. Many `SECURITY DEFINER` functions across this repository look up a record by its own bare `id` (no tenant scoping in the `WHERE` clause, by necessity — the caller doesn't yet know which tenant owns it), THEN perform the actor's authority check, and on denial raise an exception whose message text embeds the record's own real `tenant_id`, e.g. `insufficient_authority: identity % lacks DEPLOY:Approve (%) for tenant %`. Live-reproduced this checkpoint: an identity with zero role assignments or tenant membership anywhere on the platform, calling `app.approve_dedicated_deployment_qualification`/`app.set_deployment_provisioning_status` (`IAE-032`), `app.approve_region_assignment` (`IAE-033`), or `app.set_scaling_recommendation_status` (`IAE-034`) against a record UUID belonging to a tenant it has no relationship to, receives the record's real, genuine `tenant_id` verbatim in the raised exception's own text — before its own authorization has been evaluated. Failure paths also differ observably by whether the row exists at all (`no_data_found`/`check_violation` vs. `insufficient_privilege`), a working existence oracle on top of the ownership oracle.

This is taxonomy class C-05 (`docs/standards/RECURRING_DEFECT_TAXONOMY.md` — "permission check ordered after a read that already discloses data; failure paths differing observably by row existence"). Confirmed via repository-wide grep that the exact message-template shape (`raise exception '...for tenant %', ..., v_record.tenant_id`) occurs **2,087 times** across the migration history, beginning in Phase 6 — Group 8 faithfully reproduced an already-established, seemingly repository-wide-accepted convention rather than introducing something new. Exploitability requires the caller to already possess a valid, non-enumerable v4 UUID for a record belonging to a tenant it has no relationship to (via some other leak channel — a URL, a log line, a support ticket); no field beyond the bare tenant UUID is disclosed, and tenant UUIDs are not otherwise treated as secret anywhere in this application (they routinely appear in JWTs/URLs for legitimate members).

**Status `OPEN`**, Low severity — narrow blast radius (a single, non-secret UUID field, requiring an out-of-band leak of the record id first), and not a Group-8-specific regression (2,000+ pre-existing occurrences across many already-`VERIFIED` phases/batches). **Not fixed by this checkpoint** — patching only the ~8 Group-8 occurrences the review happened to name would leave the other 2,000+ instances (and the underlying pattern) untouched, exactly the "a finding fixed only where it was found is an incomplete fix" trap `RECURRING_DEFECT_TAXONOMY.md` §5 itself warns against; a real fix requires a single, repository-wide sweep (e.g., a shared helper that raises a tenant-blind `insufficient_authority`/`not_found` message, or reordering every affected function to check existence-and-authority together before ever reading `tenant_id` into an interpolated string) — genuinely out of scope for a four-capability batch fix pass. Owner: a dedicated future repository-wide hardening task, scoped to sweeping every `raise exception` that interpolates a looked-up record's own `tenant_id` (or any other cross-tenant field) into message text before the caller's own authority over that specific tenant has been established.

**Reconfirmed and re-measured (`HDN-378`, Prompt 378 Security Hardening, infra/attack-surface investigation lens):** repository-wide count of the exact message-template shape re-run directly against current `HEAD` — **2,335 occurrences** (up from 2,087 at original disclosure), confirming the pattern is still growing, not shrinking: every capability added since Group 8 (`HDN-372` through `HDN-377`) followed the same established, unexamined convention rather than closing it. A 10-site reachability sample (drawn across distinct, unrelated capabilities — deployment, case management, procurement, finance, ticketing) found **10/10** genuinely tenant-blind (looked up by bare `id`, tenant derived only afterward, disclosed in the eventual authority-denial message), confirming this is not a narrow or stale class. Of the 2,335 total occurrences, 871 (37%) use a caller-supplied `p_tenant_id` (not a disclosure — filtered from the reachable count), leaving **~1,464 genuine lookup-derived occurrences**. Severity re-assessed and **held at Low, unchanged** — the original narrow-blast-radius reasoning (single non-secret UUID field, requires an out-of-band record-id leak first, tenant UUIDs already appear routinely in JWTs/URLs) still holds and is not narrowed by the larger confirmed count. **Still not fixed by this checkpoint** — deliberately not touching newly-added call sites in isolation, which would repeat exactly the "fixed only where found" trap already named above. Owner and scope unchanged.

### ISS-2026-147 — Batch 3's own two Tier C-disclosed findings (zero test coverage for the 9 `/api/v1` REST route handlers; `IAE-013`'s own per-connector execution-log filtering claim mismatch) were never registered in this file, breaking the discipline every later Phase 9 batch followed (Phase 9, `CG-S14-IAE-036`, Prompt 364 Integrated Verification, full regression/parity lens, item 1 `RESOLVED` at `HDN-376`, item 2 still `OPEN`, Low)

Found by `CG-S14-IAE-036`'s own REST/GraphQL parity and full-regression lens while re-verifying Phase 9's own closure discipline against the whole merged 34-capability system. `docs/build-log/phase-09/00_EXECUTION_INDEX.md` §14 (Batch 3, Prompts 337-341) itself already disclosed both findings at the time — "disclosed, not fixed" — but neither was ever promoted into this file the way every subsequent batch's own disclosed residuals were (`ISS-2026-143` through `146`), leaving Phase 9's own known-issue register incomplete relative to its own build-log record.

**Item 1 (Medium) — `RESOLVED` at `HDN-376`.** `IAE-009`/`IAE-010`/`IAE-011` (Public/Customer/Vendor API, Prompts 337-339) together expose 9 real `/api/v1` REST route handlers; zero of them had their own `.test.ts` route-level test file. This never meant the underlying RPCs were untested — every RPC each route calls is exercised by its own capability's `scripts/db-tests/*.sql` file — but the HTTP-layer concerns (request parsing, header/auth extraction, response shaping, error-code mapping to HTTP status) had zero dedicated coverage. **Closed at `HDN-376`** (Prompt 376, API Compatibility Audit, whose own charter squarely covers this): a shared, reusable fetch-stubbing test harness (`tests/api/v1/support/rpc-fetch-stub.ts` — `authorizeApiV1Request()` internally constructs a real, non-injectable Supabase client with no local PostgREST/Supabase stack available in this environment, so the harness stubs `globalThis.fetch` at the network boundary while every route's own real request parsing/validation/response-shaping logic runs for real) plus 44 new tests across all 9 route handlers (`tests/api/v1/*.test.ts`), covering auth denial, request validation, RPC-error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping, and success paths per route. Found and fixed 2 real route-level defects in the process (`ISS-2026-211`, `ISS-2026-212`).

**Item 2 (Low) — still `OPEN`.** `IAE-013` (n8n Integration, Prompt 341) claims its own per-connector execution-log filtering scopes correctly by connector id; Batch 3's own Tier C review found the claim's supporting evidence narrower than stated (a documentation/evidence-completeness mismatch, not a live-reproduced authorization bypass — the filtering itself was not shown to leak across connectors, only under-evidenced relative to what the build log asserted). **Not fixed by `HDN-376`** — outside its own API-compatibility charter (n8n execution-log evidence is an Automation/Integration-domain documentation gap, not an API contract). Owner: a documentation-evidence follow-up on `IAE-341.md`.

Confirmed: Phase 9 has zero load/performance-test evidence anywhere — not the reporting engine, dashboard builder, materialized-view refresh, scheduled reports, automation rule engine, the whole `/api/v1` surface, the webhook delivery worker, any AI-governed dispatch path, or enterprise IAM/monitoring/DR — at any declared target volume, and unlike Phase 8's own identical gap, this had never been disclosed for Phase 9 until this checkpoint.

**Status `OPEN`**, Medium severity (matches `ISS-2026-141`'s own disposition exactly — a genuine, disclosed evidence gap, not a live-reproduced defect; does not by itself block a `_VERIFIED` closure state per this repository's own standing rule that a disclosed non-Critical/High gap with a named owner is non-blocking). **Not fixed by this checkpoint** — building a real load/performance-test harness for 34 capabilities' worth of routes/RPCs is a substantial, dedicated undertaking, genuinely outside `IAE-036`'s own verification-only charter.
